brand.company_name: ESG Astraa (the site's SERP title and page titles use "Esgastraa"; body copy and blog use "ESG Astraa")
brand.what_they_do:
ESG Astraa sells ESG advisory and a SaaS platform together, aimed at Indian companies. I could not open esgastraa.com directly (see uncertainties), so everything below comes from search-engine snippets of the site.

1) ADVISORY. Mission line: "turn ESG complexity into strategic advantage through advisory, reporting, and platform expertise" (https://esgastraa.com/). Services sit in three groups:
- Strategy & Advisory: ESG Strategy & Transformation, BRSR & ESG Compliance, Carbon Advisory & Credits, ESG Risk & Governance, Sustainable Finance Advisory, ESG Data & Intelligence.
- Finance & Risk: ESG Financial Analysis, ESG Tax Advisory, Green Finance & Bonds, ESG-Linked Financing, ESG Due Diligence, Cyber Risk & ESG Privacy.
- Governance & Social: Governance & Board Advisory, ESG Policy Frameworks.
The engagement process is Assess, Strategise, Measure, Sustain (https://esgastraa.com/).

2) PLATFORM. The "Smart ESG Platform" claims:
- tracking of "1000+ ESG KPIs with real-time data ingestion and automated validation"
- modules: Audit Automation, Reporting Dashboard, Data Management, Compliance Tracker
- Scope 3 and supplier ESG with "automated onboarding"
- science-based target setting and decarbonisation roadmaps
- "automated disclosures for SASB, TCFD, ESRS, CSRD, and CDP in seconds"
- framework alignment to BRSR, GRI, SASB and the UN SDGs
- headline claim that it "cuts BRSR reporting time by 70%… 3 weeks in under a day"
(all from https://esgastraa.com/)

Sectors named on the site: Manufacturing, Energy & Power, Healthcare & Pharma, Infrastructure & Real Estate (https://esgastraa.com/).

3) PRODUCT UNDER BUILD (public GitHub mirror, https://github.com/singhpratham19/esgastraa-tool):
- Brief line: "Astraa does the work; the human approves it; the trail shows it."
- Three layers: a record layer (collection, lineage, approval, versioning, filing); in-app AI on Gemini that reads documents and drafts proposals with approve/edit/reject gates and confidence scores tied to sources; and an MCP bridge to Claude, ChatGPT or Copilot for scenario and board narrative.
- 55 screens, including a CBAM wizard, supplier portal, materiality survey and audit log; seed dataset "Novaferro", a manufacturer.
- Frameworks in the brief: BRSR, GHG inventories, CBAM, CCTS.
- Stated go-to-market rule: "Sell CBAM first."

The owner's private repo "astraa-build" (seen only through authenticated GitHub search, not public) has the description: "ESG Astraa — collect activity data once, serve BRSR, GHG inventories, CBAM and CCTS from one store."
target_customers: Stated on the site: companies doing BRSR and ESG compliance in India (https://esgastraa.com/). SEBI requires BRSR from the top 1,000 listed companies by market cap. BRSR Core assessment or assurance applies to the top 500 from FY2025-26 and the top 1,000 from FY2026-27 (SEBI circular of 28 Mar 2025, referenced at https://www.sebi.gov.in/sebi_data/faqfiles/apr-2025/1745399101865.pdf; phase-in per https://thefootnotes.in/articles/brsr-core-assurance-fy2026-27-checklist and https://www.orfonline.org/research/enhancing-the-interoperability-of-india-s-business-sustainability-reporting-with-international-standards)
Stated on the site: Manufacturing, Energy & Power (power generation and utilities), Healthcare & Pharma, Infrastructure & Real Estate (https://esgastraa.com/)
Stated in the product brief: Indian manufacturers, exporters and listed mid-market companies (https://github.com/singhpratham19/esgastraa-tool)

Inferred from the brief's 'Sell CBAM first' and its CBAM wizard: Indian exporters of CBAM goods (steel, aluminium, cement and so on) to the EU. CBAM's definitive period started 1 Jan 2026, and certificate sales start 1 Feb 2027 (https://taxation-customs.ec.europa.eu/news/reminder-cbam-goes-live-1-january-2026-2025-12-23_en, https://taxation-customs.ec.europa.eu/document/download/013fa763-5dce-4726-a204-69fec04d5ce2_en?filename=CBAM_Questions+and+Answers.pdf)

Inferred from the CCTS blog post and the brief: the 490 CCTS obligated entities with notified GHG emission intensity targets (282 entities in aluminium, cement, chlor-alkali and pulp & paper notified Oct 2025; 208 in refineries, petrochemicals, textiles and secondary aluminium notified 13 Jan 2026) (https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2217239&reg=3&lang=2)

Inferred buyer personas: Head of Sustainability/ESG, CFO or finance controller, Company Secretary or compliance lead (who owns BRSR in the annual report), and export or commercial heads (who face CBAM price pressure; the brief cites 15-22% price concessions) (https://github.com/singhpratham19/esgastraa-tool)
Inferred from the Scope 3 'automated onboarding' module and the supplier portal: suppliers in large companies' value chains
geographies: India: primary market. The site, blog and brief are all India-focused (https://esgastraa.com/, https://esgastraa.com/insights/blogs/2, https://github.com/singhpratham19/esgastraa-tool)

European Union: regulatory destination for Indian exporters through CBAM, and the site claims ESRS/CSRD disclosures (https://esgastraa.com/). This is inferred as a secondary market; there is no evidence of EU customers.

No office address, city or legal entity could be found online. Searches on Zaubacorp, Crunchbase and Tracxn returned nothing for ESG Astraa or Esgastraa (https://www.zaubacorp.com/ESG-SOLUTIONS-PRIVATE-LIMITED-U40108GJ2022PTC135958 is an unrelated company).
brand.positioning:
Messaging as indexed: a hybrid of advisory and platform that "turn[s] ESG complexity into strategic advantage through advisory, reporting, and platform expertise" across "compliance, climate action, governance, and measurable sustainability outcomes" (https://esgastraa.com/). Proof claim: "cuts BRSR reporting time by 70%" ("3 weeks in under a day"). Breadth claim: "1000+ ESG KPIs" and multi-framework disclosures (BRSR, GRI, SASB, SDGs, TCFD, ESRS/CSRD, CDP). Thought leadership leans on India's carbon market: the blog post "The Carbon Turning Point for Indian Business", 4 June 2026 (https://esgastraa.com/insights/blogs/2).

Product positioning from the build repos is sharper and differs from the site:
- "collect activity data once, serve BRSR, GHG inventories, CBAM and CCTS from one store" (private astraa-build repo description)
- AI that does the work under human approval with full data lineage: "Astraa does the work; the human approves it; the trail shows it" (https://github.com/singhpratham19/esgastraa-tool)
- CBAM as the wedge ("Sell CBAM first") because exporters feel the financial pain and hold budget

Gap (my inference): the website reads as a broad ESG consultancy with a generic platform. The product strategy is a narrow India-compliance data spine (BRSR + CCTS + CBAM) with AI and audit lineage. Few Indian competitors span all three Indian or India-relevant regimes in one ledger. The Sustainability Cloud, Oren and Climes each publish content on BRSR, CBAM and CCTS, so the differentiator would need to be "one activity-data store, human-approved AI, evidence lineage" rather than coverage alone.

Local repo note: singhpratham19/esgtools ("ESG Impact OS") covers GHG Scope 1-3, BRSR, CSRD/ESRS, GRI, SASB, TCFD/IFRS S2, CDP and Climatiq factors. A grep found no CBAM or CCTS references, so CBAM/CCTS capability lives in the newer repos, not this one.

Oren (Oren Sustainability Hub): BRSR buyer's guide, XBRL, CCTS content (https://www.orennow.com/blog/best-software-for-brsr-reporting-comprehensive-guide-for-sustainability-reporting-in-india, https://www.orennow.com/blog/carbon-credits)
Sprih: India carbon and ESG platform (http://www.sprih.com/blogs/sebis-value-chain-relaxation-prioritizing-lasting-impact-over-ease-of-compliance/)

Newtral / Noa: BRSR drafting with BRSR Core evidence (https://newtral.io/frameworks/brsr)

Sentra.world: carbon accounting for industrial manufacturing, BRSR (https://sentra.world/)
Bharat Carbon: CCTS target-setting and carbon accounting (https://www.bharatcarbon.earth/)

CBAM specialists for Indian exporters: GreenSutra (https://greensutra.in/services/cbam-solutions/), CbamTrack (https://cbamtrack.com/), Encarbonsys (https://encarbonsys.com/cbam-blog/cbam-india-exporters-guide-2026.html), Seasaw (https://seasaw.ai/resources/cbam-india-exporters/), o2log (https://o2log.com/services/cbam-reporting.html)

CCTS/MRV tools: Climate Decode TerraNova (https://climate-decode.com/markets/india-ccts), CarbonNeeti (https://carbonneeti.com/blog/ccts-india-2025-2026-complete-guide), Green Curve (https://greencurve.solutions/ccts)

Global platforms benchmarked in the repo README: Watershed, Persefoni, Greenly (https://watershed.com/platform/measure, https://www.persefoni.com/business/carbon-footprint-measurement-analytics, https://greenly.earth/en-us/products/carbon-footprint); also SAP Green Ledger in the CBAM context (https://www.savictech.com/insights/eu-cbam-india-exporters-sap-sustainability-2026/)

Consultancies competing for the advisory side: PwC India (https://www.pwc.in/consulting/esg-consulting.html), Grant Thornton Bharat (https://www.grantthornton.in/services/esg-risk-consulting/esg-consulting-services/), KPMG India, SES (https://www.sesgovernance.com/brsr-guide), Astrum (https://www.astrum.in/what-we-do/esg-consulting-services/), Consultivo (https://consultivo.in/social-sustainability/esg-environmental-social-governance/)

Name collision, not a functional competitor, but it competes for the brand SERP: Astra ESG Solutions by Grand View Research, an ESG scores/data/consulting business with LinkedIn and PR Newswire presence (https://astra.grandviewresearch.com/, https://in.linkedin.com/company/astra-esg-solutions)
existing_content: Homepage with services, sectors, process, platform features and an unnamed testimonial-style claim ('cuts BRSR reporting time by 70%') (https://esgastraa.com/)

Insights / blog section, described as 'strategic ESG perspectives, compliance updates, and practical advisory thinking from the ESG Astraa team'. Only one post was found indexed: 'The Carbon Turning Point for Indian Business: The Indian Carbon Market Is No Longer a Future Event', dated 4 June 2026, covering the Indian Carbon Market Portal launch at Prakriti 2026 and CCTS (https://esgastraa.com/insights/blogs/2). The numeric slug /2 implies at least one other post, which was not found indexed.

Case-study PDF 'Rewriting the Fashion Equation' about H&M Group, based on H&M's public data (FY2024 Scope 1+2 down 41%, 96% renewable electricity, etc.). It reads as a desk-research case, not a client engagement (https://esgastraa.com/case-studies/H&M.pdf)
No white papers, webinars, YouTube channel, podcast, newsletter, LinkedIn company page, Instagram, X, Medium or Substack presence found (searches for each returned nothing attributable to ESG Astraa)
Public GitHub mirror with the full product brief, design laws, 55-screen map, AI spec and build order. It is indexed and appears in brand searches (https://github.com/singhpratham19/esgastraa-tool)

Other public repos under the same GitHub owner that appear related: esg-astraa-nextjs, astraa ('esg. tool'), astra ('esgtool'), esg ('esg website'), esgtools ('esg software env') (https://github.com/singhpratham19)
brand.seo_observations:
The footprint is very small: the site is indexed, but it is visible only for brand searches.

1) Indexed URLs. A site:esgastraa.com search surfaced only three URLs: the homepage, /insights/blogs/2 and /case-studies/H&M.pdf. No About, team, pricing, solution or sector pages surfaced as separate results, so those sections are probably homepage sections or not indexed (inference).

2) Title tags. The homepage SERP title is just "Esgastraa", with no category keyword (BRSR, ESG software, carbon accounting, CBAM, CCTS). The brand is spelled two ways: "Esgastraa" in titles, "ESG Astraa" in copy. The blog URL showed up once as "Esgastraa" and once with its real headline, which suggests client-side or default meta titles (inference). The PDF's indexed title is "1 www.esgastraa.com Rewriting the Fashion Equation", meaning no document title metadata. The PDF filename contains an ampersand ("H&M.pdf"). Blog slugs are numeric (/insights/blogs/2), not keyword slugs.

3) Category rankings. ESG Astraa did not appear for any non-brand category search I ran:
- "best BRSR reporting software India 2026": The Sustainability Cloud, Oren, ZeroCarbon, Newtral, Breathe ESG, Sentra
- "ESG software India carbon accounting platform for manufacturers": KeyESG, Climes, Tracxn, TSC, Sentra, GroundESG, Bharat Carbon
- "CBAM compliance software for Indian exporters": GreenSutra, TSC, CbamTrack, Seasaw, o2log, Encarbonsys
- "CCTS compliance software India": Oren, Climate Decode, CarbonNeeti, Green Curve
- "Credibl ESG platform India BRSR": Credibl dominates; ESG Astraa absent
Competitors win these SERPs with comparison and listicle content ("Best CBAM Software in India 2026", "Carbon Accounting Software in India (2026): An Honest Comparison", "Sprih vs Breathe ESG").

4) The one non-brand hit. The CCTS blog post appeared, about eighth, for the timely news query "Indian Carbon Market portal launched 2026 CCTS trading start GHG emission intensity targets notified entities". It also appeared for "Astraa" + BRSR/CBAM/CCTS. Timely India-regulation news is the only proven organic entry point.

5) Off-site mentions and backlinks. Excluding the domain, the only search result citing "esgastraa.com" was the GitHub mirror. There is no Crunchbase, Tracxn, Zaubacorp, OneStopESG (which relaunched 28 Sep 2026 with 1,600+ companies) or ensun listing found, and no press or PR. I could not measure backlinks: no Ahrefs, Semrush or Search Console access, and no search volumes were measured.

6) Name collisions dilute the brand SERP:
- "ESG Astra" and "Astraa ESG" queries are dominated by Astra ESG Solutions (Grand View Research; astra.grandviewresearch.com, LinkedIn, PR Newswire)
- linkedin.com/company/astraa is an unrelated data-analytics firm (6,628 followers per snippet)
- astraa.co.uk ("astraa-ai") is an Edinburgh AI vision-security company
- Indonesian Astra group ESG pages also compete
- No indexed results found for esgastraa.in or esgastraa.ai. Registration status is unknown (WHOIS not checked).

7) Brand SERP hygiene risk. The public GitHub mirror ranks for "ESG Astraa" queries and exposes internal strategy ("Sell CBAM first", 15-22% price-concession framing, build package for Claude Code).

8) Accuracy check on the blog, based on a snippet only. The blog reportedly says CCTS covers "490 entities across nine hard-to-abate sectors". PIB says "nearly 490 obligated entities across seven energy-intensive sectors" (https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2243377&reg=3&lang=1), and secondary sources say eight or nine. Aligning with the PIB wording would protect credibility.
brand.aeo_observations:
An AI answer engine would very likely not mention or recommend ESG Astraa for any category question today.

1) Brand-only recognition. The search tool's AI summarizer could describe ESG Astraa only when the exact brand string was in the query ("ESG Astraa", "ESGAstraa", "Astraa" + ESG/BRSR/CCTS). For "ESG Astraa founder OR CEO" it said it "could not find any company specifically called ESG Astraa" and listed unrelated Astra companies. For "ESG Astraa LinkedIn" it returned Astra ESG Solutions (Grand View Research) and the unrelated Astraa analytics firm.

2) Absent from category answers. For "best BRSR reporting software India 2026", "ESG software India carbon accounting", "CBAM software for Indian exporters" and "CCTS compliance software", the AI summaries named TSC, Oren, Noa/Newtral, Ecodrisil, Breathe ESG, Climes, Sprih, Updapt, StepChange, Sentra, GroundESG, Bharat Carbon, Credibl, GreenSutra, CbamTrack, Climate Decode and CarbonNeeti. ESG Astraa did not appear in any of them.

3) Entity confusion. For "what is ESG Astraa reviews pricing demo" and "esgastraa.in OR esgastraa.ai", the AI summary described ESG Astraa as "a build package… to start building the product in Claude Code", taken from the GitHub mirror. Answer engines may currently describe the brand as a GitHub dev project rather than a company. Separately, one summary framed the H&M PDF as evidence of "their work with major global brands", a misattribution risk.

4) Missing entity signals. There is no indexed About or team page, no named founders, no LinkedIn company page, no Crunchbase, Tracxn or MCA-visible legal entity, no Wikipedia/Wikidata entry, no third-party reviews (G2, Capterra, SoftwareAdvice searches found nothing), and no directory listings. I could not verify Organization or FAQ schema because the site could not be fetched.

5) Self-check on model knowledge. My own training data (cutoff June 2026) contains no knowledge of ESG Astraa. This is an observation about one model and does not predict other engines.

6) Positive. The answer engine did extract and paraphrase the CCTS blog accurately: portal launch at Prakriti 2026 and MRV scope. Timely, fact-dense India-regulation explainers are extractable and could be cited.

7) Overall: low AEO visibility (my qualitative estimate). Proxies: absence from AI summaries on 6 category queries, presence only on exact-brand queries, and AI conflation with Astra-branded entities.
brand.inferences_and_uncertainties:
ACCESS LIMITS (read first):
- The environment's network policy blocked WebFetch for esgastraa.com, web.archive.org, icapcarbonaction.com, esgtoday.com and taxation-customs.ec.europa.eu. To allow them, change Network access in the cloud environment's settings (environment menu in the session title bar, then Edit) and add these hosts or pick a broader access level.
- The Firecrawl MCP returned "insufficient credits"; more credits are needed to scrape.
- A direct curl attempt was denied by the permission system and was not retried.
- So every website fact above comes from WebSearch result snippets and AI-generated summaries of esgastraa.com, not first-hand page reads. Wording may be paraphrased, page structure is unknown, and testimonials, client names, pricing, CTAs, footer, address, social links and schema markup could NOT be verified.
- GitHub MCP access was limited to singhpratham19/esgtools. The public mirror was read through raw.githubusercontent.com and github.com via WebFetch. The private repo "astraa-build" was seen only as a search-result description; it is not public evidence.

FOUNDERS / TEAM: Not found publicly. All ESG Astraa repos (esgastraa-tool, esg-astraa-nextjs, astraa, astra, esgtools, private astraa-build) belong to GitHub account singhpratham19. I did not link that handle to any named person; searches for that link returned unrelated people.

UNVERIFIED CLAIMS:
- "1000+ ESG KPIs", "70% faster BRSR (3 weeks to under a day)" and automated SASB/TCFD/ESRS/CSRD/CDP disclosures "in seconds" are marketing claims with no evidence found.
- My inference: these go beyond what the esgtools repo implements (no CBAM/CCTS; seeded demo data). They may be aspirational or rely on the newer repos.
- Whether a separate testimonial name exists could not be verified.

INFERENCES (labelled):
(a) The business is early stage and pre-scale or pre-launch. Basis: three indexed URLs, no third-party mentions, no social presence, product still being built in public and private repos with seed datasets (Novaferro in the mirror; the esgtools demo is an Indian industrial manufacturer with Mumbai HQ and Pune, Nashik and Chennai plants).
(b) Advisory probably funds or opens doors for the platform (a hybrid like Credibl).
(c) The strategic wedge has shifted from BRSR (site) to CBAM plus CCTS (brief: "Sell CBAM first"). The website does not yet reflect that.

REGULATORY FACTS (verified as of 2026-10-01 via search snippets of primary sources; full pages not readable):
- CBAM definitive period since 1 Jan 2026; 50-tonne annual threshold; certificate sales from 1 Feb 2027; first declaration and surrender by 30 Sep 2027 for 2026 imports (EC Q&A and news). The 50 t threshold's legal basis, Reg (EU) 2025/2083, comes from secondary sources (https://cbamguide.com/compliance/de-minimis/).
- Indian Carbon Market Portal launched 21 Mar 2026 at Prakriti 2026 (PIB).
- GEI targets: 282 entities in four sectors (Oct 2025) plus 208 entities on 13 Jan 2026, giving 490 (PIB). The sector count is inconsistent: PIB says seven, secondary sources say eight or nine; some secondary sources also list iron & steel, which I could not confirm.
- NOT verified: whether CCC trading on power exchanges has actually started (a secondary source said it was expected around Oct 2026: https://www.saurenergy.com/solar-energy-news/indias-carbon-market-edges-toward-its-first-trade-12482615), and the CERC March 2026 trading regulations (secondary only).
- BRSR: top 1,000 listed entities; BRSR Core "assessment or assurance" per the SEBI circular of 28 Mar 2025; top 500 in FY2025-26 and top 1,000 in FY2026-27 (secondary sources for the phase-in); value-chain disclosures voluntary. A pending SEBI consultation on further BRSR changes was mentioned by IEEFA/ORF; its final status was not verified.

NO SEARCH VOLUMES OR BACKLINK COUNTS were measured; none are claimed.

key_findings.finding: VERIFICATION LIMIT: WebFetch was blocked by the egress proxy for searchenginejournal.com, semrush.com, ahrefs.com, tryprofound.com, seerinteractive.com, arxiv.org, developers.google.com and sebi.gov.in, and Firecrawl had no credits. So every finding below comes from WebSearch result summaries of the named pages, not from reading the pages myself. Treat the numbers as reported figures and re-check them against the primary page before quoting them in a white paper.

Google's official position (guide published 15 May 2026, 'Optimizing your website for generative AI features on Google Search'): AI Overviews and AI Mode are 'rooted in our core Search ranking and quality systems'. Optimising for them is 'still SEO'. They use RAG and query fan-out over the Search index. You do not need to chunk content, add special schema, or create AI text files such as llms.txt.

Ranking in the top 10 matters less for AI Overview citations than it used to. In Ahrefs' March 2026 study (863k keywords, ~4M AIO citations), only 38% of cited pages ranked in the organic top 10 for the same query, down from 76% in its July 2025 study. About 31% ranked 11-100 and about 31% ranked below 100. Fan-out sub-queries pull in pages that rank for related questions.

BrightEdge (Feb 2025 to Feb 2026): the share of B2B Technology queries showing an AI Overview rose from 36% to 82%. Overlap between AIO citations and the B2B-tech top 10 is in the low 20s%. In practice, most B2B buyer queries now get an AI answer that cites pages beyond page one.

Seer Interactive (Sep 2025; 3,119 informational queries, 42 organisations): on queries with an AI Overview, organic CTR fell 61% (1.76% to 0.61%) and paid CTR fell 68%. Brands cited inside the AIO earned 35% more organic clicks and 91% more paid clicks than uncited brands. Being cited is now how you protect clicks.

Scale: at Google I/O 2026, AI Overviews were reported at over 2.5B monthly users and AI Mode at over 1B monthly users. AI Mode queries are about 3x longer than classic search queries (Kevin Indig, H1 2026).

India context: Google rolled out AI Mode to everyone in India on 8 July 2025 and added Hindi in Sep 2025. Sam Altman said India has 100M weekly ChatGPT users and is OpenAI's second-largest market (Feb 2026). Indian ESG buyers are already searching through answer engines.

B2B buying behaviour (G2 survey of 1,076 B2B software buyers, March 2026; published 15 Apr 2026): 51% now start software research with an AI chatbot more often than with Google, up from 36% seven months earlier. 69% chose a different vendor than planned because of chatbot guidance.

How ChatGPT picks citations (Ahrefs, 1.4M prompts): only about 50% of the URLs ChatGPT retrieves end up cited. The strongest predictor is how semantically close the page title is to ChatGPT's hidden fan-out sub-queries (0.602 for cited pages vs 0.484 for uncited). Natural-language URL slugs were cited 89.78% of the time vs 81.11% for other slugs. Reddit pages make up 67.8% of retrieved-but-uncited URLs and are cited only 1.93% of the time.

ChatGPT's link to Bing is weakening. In 2024 Seer found 87% of SearchGPT citations matched Bing's top 10. Later 2026 reporting (attributed to Profound) says Bing alignment fell while Google alignment rose, so ranking in both Bing and Google matters. I could not verify the Profound numbers.

Platforms behave differently. Semrush (230k+ prompts over 13 weeks): Perplexity's citations overlap Google's top 10 by about 91% at domain level and 82% at URL level, vs 53.68% and 35.41% for Google AI Mode. Reddit and LinkedIn are top-5 cited domains on ChatGPT, AI Mode and Perplexity.

Citations rarely carry across engines. Profound's study of 680M citations (Aug 2024 to Jun 2025) found only about 11% of domains are cited by both ChatGPT and Perplexity. Kevin Indig's H1 2026 report says 91% of citations appear in only one of ChatGPT, Perplexity or AI Overviews. A white paper has to be promoted through several channels, not tuned for a single engine.

Claude: Anthropic lists Brave Search as its web-search subprocessor (added 19 Mar 2025). Third-party analyses report that 79-87% of Claude-cited URLs are in Brave's top 10. Anthropic runs three separate robots.txt user agents: ClaudeBot (training), Claude-SearchBot (search index) and Claude-User (live fetch). Blocking one does not block the others. The overlap figures are third-party estimates.

Microsoft Copilot answers are grounded in Bing's index. On 27 Feb 2026 Bing rewrote its Webmaster Guidelines to name GEO and treat 'grounding results and citations' as an eligibility outcome of their own. Bing Webmaster Tools added a free AI Performance report (public preview, 9 Feb 2026) that shows Copilot citations by URL and grounding query. It is the only first-party AI citation dashboard. Microsoft recommends IndexNow so updated pages are fetched quickly.

Ghost citations (Semrush with Kevin Indig, June 2026; 3,981 domain appearances, 115 prompts, 14 countries): about 62% of AI citations cite a domain without naming the brand. ChatGPT cites sources about 87% of the time but names brands in only about 20.7% of appearances. Gemini names brands in about 83.7% of appearances but cites only about 21.4%. White-paper statistics should carry the brand and index name in the sentence itself.

The GEO paper (Aggarwal et al., KDD 2024, arXiv:2311.09735) tested content changes on GEO-bench and found they can raise visibility in generative-engine answers by up to 40%. The best methods were Cite Sources, Quotation Addition and Statistics Addition. Keyword stuffing did not help.

Answer capsules: a Search Engine Land audit (15 domains, about 2M monthly sessions) found 72.4% of ChatGPT-cited blog posts had a self-contained answer of 40-60 words directly under the title or a question-style H2. About 91% of those capsules had no links. Capsule plus original data (34.3% of cited posts) was the strongest combination.

Position on the page matters. Kevin Indig's analysis of about 1.2M ChatGPT answers found 44.2% of citations come from the first 30% of a page's text (a 'ski ramp'). Put the headline numbers and definitions at the top of each white-paper page, not in a closing chapter.

Original data only gets cited when it is formatted as a benchmark. In a sample of 301 AI-cited pages, only 8 were primary research. Those 8 earned 8.4% of all citations, 3.3x the citation density of other pages. Narrative research reports were rarely cited. Named, measurable comparisons ('which is best / how do sectors compare') were. Annual white papers should therefore be built as ranked or comparative benchmark tables.

Schema does not cause citations. Ahrefs tracked 1,885 pages that added JSON-LD (Aug 2025 to Mar 2026) against about 4,000 controls. Changes were +2.4% on AI Mode and +2.2% on ChatGPT (both not significant) and -4.6% on AI Overviews (significant). Keep Article, Organization and Dataset markup for entity clarity and Dataset Search, but do not plan around schema as a citation lever.

FAQ rich results: Google stopped showing them on 7 May 2026, and the Search Console report and API data were removed by Aug 2026. FAQPage is still valid schema.org markup and costs nothing to keep on visible Q&A blocks. Do not expect a Google SERP feature from it.

There is no evidence llms.txt helps. Google's John Mueller said 'no AI system currently uses llms.txt', and Gary Illyes said Google will not support it (July 2025). SE Ranking found 10.13% adoption across 300k domains and no correlation with AI citations. Adding the file costs little, but it should not count as a tactic.

Freshness: Ahrefs' study of about 17M citations across ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, Copilot and AIO found AI-cited pages are about 25.7% fresher than Google organic results. ChatGPT-cited URLs were 393-458 days newer. Publish white papers as versioned HTML with visible 'last updated' dates and refresh them quarterly. Figures such as '+47% from adding a Last-updated date' come only from aggregators and are unverified.

Brand mentions beat links. In Ahrefs' 75k-brand correlation study, branded web mentions correlated with AI Overview visibility at r=0.664 and backlinks at r=0.218. YouTube mentions were the strongest single correlate (r about 0.737). This is correlation, not causation, but it supports earning coverage in Indian business media and YouTube for each report.

Most-cited domains: YouTube is the most-cited domain in AI Overviews at about 22.9% (Ahrefs Brand Radar, Sep 2026), but only about 1.8% in ChatGPT. LinkedIn is reported as the most-cited domain for professional queries, having more than doubled its citation frequency between Nov 2025 and Feb 2026 (Profound). Wikipedia and Reddit together exceed 25% of US ChatGPT citations (5W). For B2B ESG, LinkedIn (company page plus executive articles) and YouTube walkthroughs are the highest-leverage third-party channels.

Self-ranking listicles backfire. Scrunch (about 10k cited URLs across 7 AI surfaces, May-June 2026; published 24 Sep 2026) found self-ranked vendors were recommended only slightly more often (4% to 7%). A Lily Ray / Search Engine Land study found that when a brand's own 'best X' listicle was cited by AI Overviews, the brand was left out of the recommendation 69% of the time. Avoid self-ranked 'best ESG software India' pages and publish transparent, methodology-led benchmarks instead.

Review sites act as a gate for inclusion more than as a cited source. One 2026 study of 40 B2B SaaS categories found G2 and Capterra almost never appear as ChatGPT citations, yet nearly all recommended tools had G2 and Capterra reviews. In AI Overviews, G2 took about 23.1% of review-platform citations. ESG Astraa needs complete G2 and Capterra India profiles to qualify for shortlists. These figures come from vendor and agency studies.

Gated and PDF-only white papers are invisible to retrieval. AI crawlers (OAI-SearchBot, PerplexityBot, Claude-SearchBot, Googlebot) cannot submit lead forms. Google's guidance says to keep important content in textual HTML form. Publish the full report as ungated HTML (one URL per chapter, with chart data as HTML tables) and offer the designed PDF and CSV as optional downloads. The specific claims about PDF crawl frequency come from secondary sources.

Crawler access needs checking. Since 1 July 2025 Cloudflare blocks AI crawlers by default for new zones, and it expanded default blocking in Sep 2026. Make sure the CDN/WAF allows OAI-SearchBot, ChatGPT-User, PerplexityBot, Claude-SearchBot, Claude-User, Bingbot and Googlebot. Training bots (GPTBot, ClaudeBot) can be handled separately.

AI referral traffic converts well but is small. Semrush (500+ B2B topics) reports AI-search visitors convert at 4.4x the rate of organic visitors. Conductor reports AI referrals at about 1.08% of total traffic. Track chatgpt.com, perplexity.ai, copilot.microsoft.com and gemini.google.com as a separate GA4 channel, and use Bing AI Performance plus a fixed prompt panel to measure white-paper citations.

Entity building: Organization schema with sameAs links to LinkedIn, Crunchbase, G2 and Wikidata is the standard way to disambiguate a brand. A Wikidata item needs notability (independent references), so get press coverage first. Vendor claims of a ~20% AIO visibility lift from entity linking (Schema App) are unverified.

SERP test, 'what is BRSR Core': results are spread across consultancies and vendors (Schneider Perspectives, Uniqus, Benchmark Gensuite, Taxmann, India Briefing, Glocert, Treeni, Orennow, SYNE). No SEBI page appeared in the top results, even though the primary document is SEBI's Annexure I PDF. No single source dominates, which leaves room for a definitive, well-sourced HTML answer.

SERP test, 'best ESG reporting software India': results are directories (SourceForge, Capterra India) plus vendor self-listicles (thesustainabilitycloud.com held 3 slots, samcorporate, sparrowrms, zoeiesg, 4seer). The global competitors (Watershed, Persefoni, Greenly, Credibl) did not appear. There is no independent India comparison with a published methodology.

SERP test, 'how to calculate scope 3 emissions for Indian manufacturers': results are the GHG Protocol PDF, UNFCCC, Normative and generic vendor blogs. None has India-specific factors. Follow-up searches for INR-denominated spend-based (EEIO) factors and for an Indian per-tonne Category 1 steel factor returned no authoritative source. Only an open GitHub 'open-india-emission-factors' project and CEA/GHG Platform India data exist. This is the clearest gap for an India-specific, well-structured answer.

Extractable formats win on simple factual queries. For 'CEA grid emission factor 2024-25', small vendor programmatic pages (batchwise.ai 'Latest Value, 5-Year Trend', carbonneeti, reclimatize) rank alongside or above the primary CEA V21.0 PDF. They put the value in the title and present tables. The primary figure is CEA V21.0 (Dec 2025): FY2024-25 weighted average emission factor of 0.710 tCO2/MWh.

Data-led BRSR benchmarks come mostly from academia and think tanks, published as PDFs or gated. Examples: IIM Bangalore (982 FY2024-25 filings; Aug 2026), CEEW (1,258 filings on air emissions; 16 Jul 2026), NSE-CFA Institute (300 companies; Oct 2024), IIM Ahmedabad (Feb 2025), XBRL International (Feb 2024), and StepChange BRSR Barometer 2025 (800+ companies; download appears gated). No ESG software vendor runs an ungated, HTML-first annual India benchmark with downloadable sector tables.

Example of an extractable statistic that earned media pickup. IIM Bangalore found 57.1% of top-1,000 listed companies did not disclose Scope 3 in FY2024-25, and Scope 1+2 emissions rose 4.29% year on year, with 53.1% of companies reporting increases. The single stat-led headline was picked up by BusinessToday. This is the pattern ESG Astraa should copy.

BRSR data quality is a quotable, measurable gap. CEEW (Jul 2026) found particulate matter reported in more than a dozen incompatible units across BRSR filings. NSE-CFA flagged unclear data sources and inconsistent units. Running ESG Astraa's validation checks over public BRSR XBRL filings would produce a new 'data-quality / assurance-readiness' metric that nobody else publishes.

Regulatory why-now, BRSR Core. SEBI circular SEBI/HO/CFD/CFD-PoD-1/P/CIR/2025/42 (28 Mar 2025) replaced 'reasonable assurance' with 'assessment or assurance' and extends the glide path to the top 1,000 listed entities from FY2026-27. Value-chain ESG disclosure is voluntary for the top 250 from FY2025-26 and covers partners with at least 2% of purchases or sales, capped at 75% coverage. I could not fetch sebi.gov.in directly; this is confirmed only through secondary sources.

Regulatory why-now, assurance standard. ICAI has issued the Standard on Sustainability Assurance SSA 5000, reportedly effective from 1 Apr 2027 (BusinessToday, Sep 2026). Assurance-readiness content will have a second trigger in 2027. I have not seen the effective date in a primary ICAI notification.

Regulatory why-now, CCTS (India's carbon market). The GHG Emission Intensity Target Rules were notified 8 Oct 2025 (282 obligated entities in aluminium, cement, chlor-alkali and pulp and paper). A Jan 2026 amendment added 208 units (refineries, petrochemicals, textiles, secondary aluminium). Targets apply to 2025-26 and 2026-27 against an FY2023-24 baseline. A shortfall triggers environmental compensation of 2x the average CCC trading price, levied by CPCB.

Regulatory why-now, CCC trading. CERC notified its Carbon Credit Certificate trading regulations on 27 Feb 2026 (gazette 3 Mar 2026). Trading is on IEX, PXIL and HPX in monthly sessions within a floor and forbearance price band, with first trading expected around Oct 2026. The actual floor and forbearance values were not found. Published price expectations (₹250-1,500/t) are analyst estimates only.

Regulatory why-now, CBAM. The definitive period began 1 Jan 2026. A 50-tonne annual de minimis threshold now applies (Omnibus Regulation (EU) 2025/2083). Certificate sales start 1 Feb 2027. The EU-India FTA concluded in Jan 2026 gives India no CBAM exemption, only a 'technical dialogue'. Vendor blogs quote very inconsistent India default values and costs (e.g. about 2.5 tCO2/t, or €250+/t vs €65-170/t with actual data); these are unverified, which is why an authoritative CBAM benchmark would be cited.

Regulatory why-now, CSRD. Omnibus I Directive (EU) 2026/470 was published 26 Feb 2026 and entered into force 18 Mar 2026. Non-EU parents, including Indian groups, are in scope only above €450M EU net turnover plus an EU subsidiary or branch above €200M, from FY2028 with first reports in 2029. India-relevant CSRD content should be about value-chain data requests from EU customers rather than direct obligations.

India-specific benchmark anchor for steel. The Ministry of Steel's Green Steel Taxonomy (12 Dec 2024) defines green steel as below 2.2 tCO2e per tonne of finished steel, with 5/4/3-star bands at below 1.6, 1.6-2.0 and 2.0-2.2. It covers Scope 1, Scope 2 and limited Scope 3, with NISST as the MRV agency. This lets ESG Astraa publish India-anchored comparisons for steel buyers (Scope 3 Category 1) and exporters (CBAM).

Under-served question types: (1) India-specific emission factors (spend-based INR, materials, regional grid) with versioning; (2) sector benchmarks for BRSR intensity metrics (GHG per ₹ crore PPP-adjusted, water KL per ₹ crore); (3) the cost and evidence requirements of BRSR Core assessment vs assurance (only vendor cost guesses such as ₹15-25 lakh); (4) CCTS GEI targets by sector in sortable form, plus exposure to CCC prices; (5) CBAM default vs actual values for Indian production routes; (6) MSME supplier data readiness. A practitioner guide also observes that Perplexity mixes US/UK references into BRSR answers, a sign that well-structured India-context sources are scarce (low confidence).

WHITE-PAPER TACTIC CHECKLIST, drawn from the evidence above. (1) Publish ungated HTML first, one URL per chapter with a natural-language slug and a question-style H1/H2 that mirrors fan-out sub-queries. (2) Start each section with a link-free answer capsule of 40-60 words and keep key stats in the first 30% of the page. (3) Present findings as named, ranked benchmarks (sector medians, quartiles, 'which sector is best/worst') rather than narrative. (4) Write each stat as a self-contained sentence with the brand and index name and the primary source (SEBI, CEA, BEE, MoEFCC). (5) Publish the methodology, sample size and data dates, plus CSV downloads with Dataset schema. (6) Show a visible 'last updated' date, refresh quarterly, ping IndexNow, and monitor Bing AI Performance. (7) Seed LinkedIn (company page and executive articles), a YouTube walkthrough and Indian business-media coverage. (8) Use Organization/Article schema for entity clarity, not as a citation lever. Skip llms.txt and self-ranked listicles.

key_findings.finding: ACCESS LIMITS. WebFetch was blocked by the egress proxy for every domain tried (sebi.gov.in, thefootnotes.in, syntropyearth.com, kpmg.com, taxguru.in). Firecrawl returned 'insufficient credits' (402). The shared WebSearch budget ran out after 59 searches. So every fact below comes from search-engine result snippets and AI summaries of the cited pages, not from reading the full pages. SEBI primary documents (circulars, FAQs) were seen only through exchange re-circulations (NSE, BSE, MSEI) and law-firm or consultancy summaries.

BRSR is mandatory for the top 1,000 listed entities by market capitalisation. The BRSR goes to the exchange as both PDF and XBRL on the same day as the annual report; there is no separate XBRL deadline. Other listed entities, including SME-exchange companies, may file voluntarily.
key_findings.recency: NSE/BSE FAQ May 2024; still the operative filing guidance as far as found

key_findings.finding: SEBI circular SEBI/HO/CFD/CFD-PoD-1/P/CIR/2025/42 of 28 March 2025 replaced mandatory 'reasonable assurance' of BRSR Core with 'assessment or assurance'. Assessment means a third-party assessment under standards developed by the Industry Standards Forum (ISF: ASSOCHAM, CII, FICCI) in consultation with SEBI. NSE and BSE re-circulated it on 1 April 2025.

Provider rules under the March 2025 framework. The assessment or assurance provider need not be a Chartered Accountant (profession-agnostic), and the listed entity's Board must ensure the provider has the necessary expertise. There is also a conflict-of-interest bar: the provider and its associates must not sell products or provide non-assurance services, including consulting, to the listed entity or its group. Implication for ESG Astraa: as advisory plus software vendor, it cannot also act as BRSR Core assessor for its own clients, so it should position as the readiness and evidence partner.
key_findings.recency: Apr 2025; wording taken from search summaries of the BSE notice and Vinod Kothari FAQs

key_findings.finding: BRSR Core assessment/assurance glide path by market-cap rank: top 150 in FY2023-24, top 250 in FY2024-25, top 500 in FY2025-26, top 1,000 in FY2026-27. That means about 500 companies (ranks 501-1,000) get BRSR Core assessed or assured for the first time on FY2026-27 data, which is being generated now.
key_findings.recency: SEBI board memo Dec 2024; confirmed by 2026 secondary sources (thefootnotes.in, csquarecarbon.com)

key_findings.finding:
Value-chain ESG disclosures:
- Apply to the top 250 listed entities on a voluntary basis from FY2025-26. They were deferred by one year and moved from comply-or-explain to voluntary.
- Assessment or assurance of value-chain disclosures is voluntary from FY2026-27.
- The value chain means upstream and downstream partners that individually account for 2% or more of purchases or sales by value. Disclosure may be limited to partners covering 75% of purchases or sales.
- Prior-year figures are voluntary in the first year.
key_findings.recency: 28 Mar 2025 circular; SEBI board decision 18 Dec 2024

key_findings.finding: The same March 2025 circular added a voluntary leadership indicator under BRSR Principle 6: Green Credits generated or procured by the listed entity and by its top ten value-chain partners (by value of purchases and sales). It applies to BRSRs for FY2024-25 onwards.

The ISF 'Industry Standards on Reporting of BRSR Core' were notified through SEBI circular SEBI/HO/CFD/CFD-PoD-1/P/CIR/2024/177 dated 20 Dec 2024 and apply from FY2024-25. They include methodology for PPP-adjusted revenue intensity using IMF PPP conversion rates. I could not confirm whether the ISF has published a separate, dated 'standard on third-party assessment'. Sources say the ISF 'will develop' one or refer to it generically.
key_findings.recency: Dec 2024; ISF assessment-standard status unverified as of 2026-10-01

key_findings.finding: Assurance standards currently cited as acceptable for BRSR Core: ISAE 3000, ISSA 5000, or ICAI's SSAE 3000 and SAE 3410.

Around 20 Sept 2026, ICAI issued SSA 5000 (Standard on Sustainability Assurance) with a General Requirements & Framework for Sustainability Assurance Engagements.
- In force for financial years beginning on or after 1 April 2027, i.e. FY2027-28.
- SSAE 3000 and SAE 3410 will be withdrawn.
- Based on IAASB's ISSA 5000 with carve-outs on joint audits and forward-looking statements.
- Prepared in discussion with SEBI.

ICAI's Sustainability Reporting Standards Board published an Exposure Draft of a Framework for Sustainability Assurance Engagements on 20 May 2026, with comments due 19 June 2026. This was the precursor to SSA 5000.

Today's SERP for SSA 5000 is almost entirely news wires (Business Standard, ANI, Tribune, BusinessToday, plus a Hinglish Whalesbook piece). I found no company-side practical explainer. This is a low-competition, newly created query space (estimate; proxy: SERP composition).

KPMG India (Feb 2026) analysed 94 NIFTY 100 companies' FY2024-25 BRSRs:
- All obtained reasonable assurance on BRSR Core.
- 57 extended verification beyond the regulatory scope.
- 61 reported standalone and 32 consolidated.
- Nearly half restated FY24 comparatives, 16 of them to align with the Dec 2024 ISF standards.
- One construction company received a qualified opinion.

A review of NIFTY 100 FY2024-25 filings reportedly found that no company used the new ISF 'assessment' route; all chose reasonable assurance. The same source says FY2025-26 reports show Big Four affiliates, SGS, DNV, BDO, S.R. Batliboi and smaller firms as providers.

The latest large-sample BRSR studies all cover FY2024-25 or earlier. IIM Bangalore's 2026 report covers 982 of the top 1,000 companies (FY2024-25). CFA Institute's 'Current State of BRSR in Corporate India 2.0' (June 2026) covers 300 companies over FY2022-23 to FY2024-25. I found no published analysis of FY2025-26 filings: the first year the top 500 needed assessment or assurance and the first voluntary value-chain year. This is a clear data-content gap.
key_findings.recency: 2026; absence of FY2025-26 study as of 2026-10-01 (based on searches only)

key_findings.finding: FY2025-26 BRSRs are being filed now, with annual reports ahead of AGMs (typically by 30 Sept). Company-level news shows FY26 BRSRs filed with reasonable assurance on BRSR Core (e.g. Reliance Power, Data Patterns). NSE's BRSR filings page offers XBRL/CSV downloads, which makes a proprietary filing dataset feasible.

ICRA ESG Ratings (27 Jan 2026): among NSE top 200 companies, the number disclosing Scope 3 rose 58.7% over four years (75 to 119), and reported Scope 3 emissions rose 119%. Upstream categories dominate. Sector Scope 3 intensity changes: autos -10%, cement +67%, metals & mining +32%.

SEBI ESG Rating Provider (ERP) rules:
- Master Circular for ERPs issued 11 July 2025.
- April 2025 tweaks: subscriber-pays ERPs must share reports with subscribers and the rated issuer simultaneously, with two working days for issuer comments.
- SEBI set up a Working Group to review the ERP framework (Press Release 13/2026, 18 Feb 2026). Its recommendations were not found published as of 2026-10-01.

SEBI's ESG mutual fund rules (circular of 20 July 2023):
- ESG schemes must invest at least 65% of AUM in companies that report comprehensive BRSR and have assurance on BRSR Core.
- Compliance from 1 Oct 2024, with legacy schemes given until 30 Sept 2025.
- There are six ESG strategy categories, and at least 80% of assets must follow the stated strategy.
NOT VERIFIED: whether the mutual fund rule text was updated to 'assessment or assurance' after March 2025.
key_findings.recency: Jul 2023 rule; status of 2025 alignment unverified

key_findings.finding: SEBI framework for ESG debt securities (circular of 5 June 2025): covers social, sustainability and sustainability-linked bonds (green bonds are under separate rules). It requires alignment with recognised standards (e.g. ICMA), pre- and post-issuance disclosures, and third-party review to curb 'purpose-washing'.

CCPA notified the Guidelines for Prevention and Regulation of Greenwashing or Misleading Environmental Claims on 15 Oct 2024. Claims must be specific and backed by credible certification or scientific evidence, and cherry-picking is prohibited. These rules are relevant to marketing claims such as unsubstantiated performance figures.

No 2026 SEBI circular amending BRSR or BRSR Core was found in searches. Policy pressure points:
- BRSR is described as about 40% aligned with ISSB/IFRS S2 (ORF).
- IEEFA proposed a two-phase roadmap to add climate transition-plan disclosures to BRSR.
- Green Central Banking (21 Sep 2026) links BRSR disclosure quality to transition finance.
BRSR is not mandatory for unlisted companies. An MCA committee proposal to extend it remains unimplemented as far as found.
key_findings.recency: 2025-Sep 2026; sebi.gov.in could not be checked directly

key_findings.finding:
OUTDATED OR WRONG CONTENT IN RANKING PAGES (based on snippets and AI summaries, not full page reads):
- relific.io's FY2026-27 article is titled 'India's Reasonable Assurance Mandate' and describes all nine attributes as requiring reasonable assurance, although assessment has been an alternative since March 2025.
- irqs.co.in's comparison page reportedly says assessment 'is not considered as formal validation under BRSR', which contradicts the circular.
- The esg360.in post of Jan 2026 is summarised as saying value-chain assessment becomes 'mandatory' in FY2026-27; it is voluntary.
- Search summaries also surfaced claims that BRSR Core assurance must come from ICAI members, and that BRSR Core applies to the top 250 in FY2026-27. Both are wrong.

Stale filing guidance still ranks. The NSE/BSE BRSR filing FAQs (May 2024) say a 'Reasonable Assurance Certificate' must be attached, which pre-dates the March 2025 'assessment or assurance' change. Some 2026 guides still give the BRSR deadline as 'by September 30, 2025'.

The SERP for 'best BRSR reporting software India 2026' is led by vendor listicles carrying stale year labels: The Sustainability Cloud's 'Best BRSR Software in 2025' and Passionate in Marketing's '...in 2025'. Others ranking are Oren's buyer's guide, ZeroCarbon, Noa/Newtral, Breathe ESG and Sentra. ESG Astraa does not appear.

Online PPP-intensity guidance is inconsistent. ISF methodology uses IMF PPP conversion rates, yet one search summary of ranking content said SEBI requires the 'annual average exchange rate'. KPMG found restatements to align with the ISF standards. Together these point to an underserved, technical long-tail (estimate; proxy: conflicting snippets and the restatement frequency).

The nine BRSR Core attributes per SEBI Annexure I:
1. GHG footprint
2. Water footprint
3. Energy footprint
4. Embracing circularity (waste)
5. Employee wellbeing and safety
6. Gender diversity
7. Inclusive development
8. Fairness in engaging with customers and suppliers
9. Open-ness of business

Several CCTS-regulated plants belong to companies that also file BRSR, and CBAM exposure adds a third emissions regime. key_findings.finding: RESEARCH ACCESS LIMITS (read first). WebSearch returned 'budget exhausted (200/200)' and Firecrawl returned HTTP 402 (no credits), so no fresh SERP, People Also Ask or autocomplete data was collected in this session. The egress proxy blocked pib.gov.in, beeindia.gov.in, cercind.gov.in, moef.gov.in, egazette.gov.in, icapcarbonaction.com, iexindia.com, carbonneeti.com, climate-decode.com, wikipedia, zenodo, arxiv, indiankanoon and prsindia. Only github.com was reachable. The primary regulatory facts below come from official Gazette of India PDFs mirrored in a public GitHub dataset repo, which I downloaded and parsed myself. The 7 'searches' counted are GitHub repository searches. Items marked 'not verified' could not be checked against a primary source.

Phase I targets are final. MoEFCC notified the Greenhouse Gases Emission Intensity Target Rules, 2025 as G.S.R. 739(E) on 8 Oct 2025, under sections 3, 6 and 25 of the Environment (Protection) Act 1986. The draft was G.S.R. 234(E) of 16 Apr 2025. The rules cover four sectors: aluminium, cement, chlor-alkali, and pulp & paper. Baseline year is FY2023-24. Compliance years are FY2025-26 and FY2026-27. Targets are set per obligated entity in tCO2e per tonne of equivalent product. The FY2025-26 targets are pro-rated for Sept 2025 to Mar 2026. My count of registration IDs gives 282 entities: aluminium 13, cement 186 (131 clinker/integrated plants and 55 grinding units), chlor-alkali 30, pulp & paper 53.

Phase II targets are final. The GHG Emission Intensity Target (Amendment) Rules, 2025 were notified as G.S.R. 25(E), dated 13 Jan 2026 (e-gazette ID CG-DL-E-16012026-269375; the draft was dated 23 Jun 2025). They add a Second Schedule with 208 entities: secondary aluminium 3, petroleum refinery 21, petrochemical crackers 11, textiles 173. Refinery targets use tCO2e per MBBLS per NRGF. FY2025-26 targets are pro-rated for Jan to Mar 2026. Phase I and II together cover 490 entities in 7 sectors. That matches PIB's 'nearly 490 obligated entities across seven energy-intensive sectors'. It contradicts ESG Astraa's blog line 'nine hard-to-abate sectors', which needs correcting.

Iron & steel targets are in draft. MoEFCC published draft G.S.R. 517(E) on 26 Jun 2026 (uploaded 2 Jul 2026). It adds a Third Schedule of 255 iron & steel entities with FY2023-24 baselines and a FY2026-27 target only (no FY2025-26 target), and opened a 60-day objection window. Comments went to ccts.hsm-moefcc@gov.in. NOT VERIFIED: whether the final rules had been notified by 1 Oct 2026. A secondary tracker updated 19 Sep 2026 still lists steel as draft.
key_findings.recency: Draft dated 2026-06-26; final status unverified at 2026-10-01

key_findings.finding: Fertiliser had no CCTS target. Fertiliser is one of the nine sectors originally named for CCTS, yet it has no target in any of the three gazette documents. The June 2026 draft's preamble lists only the earlier notifications for 4 + 4 sectors. At least one public 'CCTS intelligence' tool says 'Textiles and Fertilisers Now Official' and 'all nine CCTS sectors now have official or near-official targets'. Both statements are wrong according to the gazette. Misinformation of this kind gives an authoritative, gazette-linked tracker an opening.

key_findings.finding:
Obligations and penalties (verbatim mechanics from G.S.R. 739(E)). Obligated entities must:
- register on the Indian Carbon Market portal
- submit documents as the BEE detailed procedure requires
- surrender banked or purchased Carbon Credit Certificates (CCCs) equal to any shortfall

CCCs issued = (target GEI − achieved GEI) × equivalent output. CCCs to buy = (achieved − target) × output. CCCs can be banked.

If an entity fails to submit documents, its achieved GEI is deemed equal to its baseline GEI when the shortfall is calculated.

If it fails to comply, CPCB imposes environmental compensation of twice the average CCC trading price in that compliance year's trading cycle. BEE sets the average price. The compensation is payable within 90 days; non-payment brings EPA penalties.

GEI targets are recommended by MoP on the advice of BEE and the National Steering Committee for Indian Carbon Market (NSCICM), and notified by MoEFCC. BEE issues CCCs.

My own calculation from the three gazette schedules (all 745 entities parsed). Method: FY2023-24 output × baseline GEI, at constant output. Refineries use throughput × NRGF. Two textile rows were corrected.
- Covered baseline emissions: about 839 MtCO2e (Phase I 359 Mt, Phase II 121 Mt, steel draft 359 Mt).
- 'Do-nothing' CCC shortfall at the FY2026-27 targets: about 36.7 Mt (Phase I 12.1, Phase II 4.6, steel 20.0).
- 310 of 745 entities face a do-nothing shortfall under 10,000 tCO2e, and 209 under 5,000 t. The median entity shortfall is about 13,700 t.
- Median shortfall by segment: textiles about 2,900 t; cement grinding units about 2,000 t; pulp & paper about 6,700 t.
- The top 75 entities (10%) hold about 65% of the total shortfall.
- 320 entities have no FY2025-26 target (all 255 steel units and 65 others).
- Odisha holds about 17.7% of baseline emissions, Chhattisgarh 12.4% and Gujarat 11.5%.
- 106 of the 255 steel units produced under 100,000 t in FY2023-24.
These are estimates, not official figures.

The secondary data has errors. The CCTS-745 manuscript reports a 767.60 MtCO2e baseline and a 34.22 Mt FY2026-27 obligation. It also misdates the notifications (for example, Phase I as '19 December 2023' and Phase III as '20 August 2024'), attributes them to the Ministry of Power instead of MoEFCC, and treats the steel draft as notified. One gazette row (Grasim Century Rayon, TXTOE127MH) prints baseline GEI as '.94244' against a 9.3345 target, which is probably a typo. Validated, lineage-linked data is a real differentiator here.

CCTS offset mechanism (CEEW issue brief, Aug 2025):
- Non-obligated entities can register projects under government-set sectoral methodologies and be issued CCCs.
- The first set has 8 methodologies: two each for energy, industry, and waste handling & disposal, and one each for agriculture and afforestation/reforestation. Transport methodologies were still awaited.
- CEEW recommends quarterly briefings to NSCICM, including annual performance reviews of Accredited Carbon Verification Agencies (ACVAs) and VVBs.
- India issued 278 million VCM credits between 2010 and 2022, 17% of global supply.
- Indian AFOLU projects average 1,689 days to register on Verra, against 623 days elsewhere in Asia.

Indian Carbon Market portal. The earlier brand research (PIB) says the portal launched at Prakriti 2026 on 21 Mar 2026, and that 208 entities were added on 13 Jan 2026, bringing the total to 490. The 13 Jan date and the 282 + 208 = 490 count match the gazette. I could not reopen the PIB page because the proxy blocked it.

Trading start date and price band: NOT VERIFIED. A secondary article said the first CCC trade was expected around Oct 2026. Public modelling tools assume a 'CERC (Terms and Conditions for Purchase and Sale of CCCs) Regulations, 2026' but use conflicting price assumptions: one uses a ₹500 floor and ₹1,500 forbearance price, another uses ₹150/₹250/₹600 'collar' scenarios. I found no primary confirmation of any official floor or ceiling. Buyers clearly want a reliable answer on CCC price, timing and exchanges.

Article 6, PAT and the voluntary market (secondary only). A Sept 2026 research log says:
- India signed a Joint Crediting Mechanism (JCM) Memorandum of Cooperation with Japan in Aug 2025. It calls this India's first live Article 6.2 bilateral framework, with no published volume.
- India's Article 6.2 eligible list has 13 activities (Feb 2023), including RE with storage, green hydrogen, green ammonia, offshore wind, CCUS and SAF.
- Fertiliser status was contested across sources, and the steel draft was criticised as weak by Climate Risk Horizons.
- BEE's PAT page shows 25.78 Mtoe of cumulative savings.
- PIB reports 97.01 MtCO2 avoided in PAT cycles I-II only.
I did not open any of the primary sources.

key_findings.finding: ACCESS LIMITS. WebSearch had already used up its 200-call session budget before this run, Firecrawl returned 'insufficient credits', and the egress proxy blocked every regulator and news domain I tried (taxation-customs.ec.europa.eu, eur-lex, consilium, gov.uk, pib.gov.in, beeindia, commerce.gov.in, policy.trade.ec.europa.eu, carbonbrief, business-standard, ieefa, gtri, competitor sites, Google Trends/autocomplete). Only GitHub was reachable. So every fact below comes from: (a) GitHub mirrors of EU legal texts (legalize-dev/legalize-eu), (b) dated GitHub knowledge bases and news archives that quote Economic Times (ET) and PIB URLs, or (c) ESG Astraa's own product brief. Confidence ratings reflect this. None of the primary pages were opened directly, and no search volumes were measured.

Regulation (EU) 2025/2083 (the CBAM Omnibus simplification), dated 8 Oct 2025, creates a single cumulative de minimis threshold of 50 tonnes net mass per importer per year for iron/steel, aluminium, fertilisers and cement. Electricity and hydrogen are excluded from it. An importer that crosses the threshold must be an authorised CBAM declarant and reports all of that year's imports. The threshold is designed to keep about 99% of embedded emissions in scope. It entered into force on the third day after publication (OJ 17 Oct 2025, per the transcription; ELI http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg/2025/2083/oj).

Authorised declarant transition: importers and indirect customs representatives that applied for authorisation by 31 March 2026 could keep importing in 2026 above the 50 t threshold while their application was pending. Importing above the threshold without authorisation triggers sanctions (new Art. 26(2a)). Splitting shipments to stay under the threshold is defined as evasion (Art. 27). Implementing Reg. (EU) 2025/2549 of 10 Dec 2025 simplified the declarant application procedures.

Money timeline: Member States start selling CBAM certificates on 1 Feb 2027 for 2026 imports. The annual declaration and surrender are due by 30 Sep of the year after import, so the first deadline is 30 Sep 2027. From 2027, declarants must hold certificates covering at least 50% of embedded emissions at each quarter-end (cut from 80%).

Certificate price (Implementing Reg. (EU) 2025/2548 of 10 Dec 2025): for 2026 it is the quarterly average of EU ETS auction clearing prices, published the week after the quarter is calculated. From 2027 it becomes a weekly average. A tracker reports Q1 2026 at EUR 75.36 (published 7 Apr 2026) and Q2 2026 at EUR 75.28 (published 6 Jul 2026), so the Q3 2026 price is due in early October 2026.

Verification rules: after 2025/2083, only actual values are verified; default values need no verification. Implementing Reg. (EU) 2025/2546 of 10 Dec 2025, applicable from 1 Jan 2026, requires a physical site visit to the installation in the first verified year and at least every two years after that. Virtual visits are allowed from year two under low-risk criteria. Materiality is 5% of total specific embedded emissions per good (CN code), and the report uses a Commission template in the CBAM Registry.

Verifier accreditation (Delegated Reg. (EU) 2025/2551 of 20 Nov 2025): EU national accreditation bodies accredit CBAM verifiers. A third-country applicant, such as an Indian verifier, may apply to any EU national accreditation body. Accredited verifiers are registered in the CBAM registry. Separately, Implementing Reg. (EU) 2025/2550 gives registry access to 'independent persons' for certification reports no earlier than 1 Dec 2026. I infer these relate to certifying carbon price paid.

Default values: Implementing Reg. (EU) 2025/2621 of 16 Dec 2025 applies from 1 Jan 2026 and must be revised by Dec 2027 at the latest. Implementing Reg. (EU) 2026/1740, adopted 20 Jul 2026 (OJ 31 Jul 2026), replaced its Annex I, and DG TAXUD published Excel v2 on 6 Aug 2026. Mark-ups on default values: 10% (2026), 20% (2027) and 30% (2028 onward) for cement, iron and steel, aluminium and hydrogen; 1% for fertilisers. Default values cannot be combined with a carbon-price deduction except through Commission-set default carbon prices.

India-specific default values, as transcribed from the 2026/1740 workbook by a third-party India CBAM calculator (base tCO2e/t, then 2026 marked-up value): hot-rolled flat steel CN 7208: 4.28, marked up 4.708; semi-finished 7207: 4.27; pig iron 7201: 2.53; unwrought aluminium 7601: 1.87 (direct only); grey Portland cement 2523 29: 1.48; urea: 2.22; ammonia: 0.99; nitric acid: 2.01; hydrogen 2804 10: 14.03, marked up 15.433. Another repo says 2026/1740 has 256 India CN-code rows. Not checked against the EU primary file.

Free allocation phase-out (CBAM factor): 97.5% in 2026, 95% in 2027, 90% in 2028, 77.5% in 2029, 51.5% in 2030, 39% in 2031, 26.5% in 2032, 14% in 2033, 0 in 2034. Only about 2.5% of the benchmark-adjusted obligation bites in 2026, and it rises steeply after 2028. The free-allocation adjustment methodology is IR (EU) 2025/2620.

Downstream extension: proposal COM(2025) 989 was tabled 17 Dec 2025 (procedure 2025/0419(COD)). It would cover about 180 steel- and aluminium-intensive downstream products (fasteners, wire, springs, household articles) from 1 Jan 2028, plus anti-avoidance rules including on the pre-consumer 'scrap loophole'. A companion Temporary Decarbonisation Fund was proposed as COM(2025) 990. The European Parliament adopted its first-reading position on 15 Sep 2026 (464-50-159). Trilogues are pending, so it is not yet law.

UK CBAM starts 1 Jan 2027. The Oct 2024 consultation response confirmed aluminium, cement, fertilisers, hydrogen and iron & steel, and dropped glass and ceramics. Secondary notes (Aug 2026) mention a GBP 50,000 12-month de minimis, no transitional phase, a first return due 31 May 2028, and electricity excluded. These details were not verified on gov.uk, which was blocked.

The UK recognises India's CCTS: Economic Times reports (8 Sep 2026 and 10 Sep 2026, quoting the Commerce Secretary) that India's carbon price will be accepted for carbon price relief under the UK CBAM. ET URLs: https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/economy/foreign-trade/uk-recognises-indias-carbon-credit-trading-scheme-relief-for-indian-exporters/articleshow/133890963.cms and .../uk-recognises-indias-ccts-carbon-price-to-be-accepted-under-cbam-regime-comm-secy/articleshow/133966978.cms

India-EU FTA: concluded 27 Jan 2026. ET reported on 29-31 Jul 2026 that it includes a separate CBAM annexure and a 'comprehensive work plan', with engagement on carbon prices paid in India and support for SMEs (ET articleshow 132748746, 132736801, 132735330). An EU trade-policy knowledge base says the Commission proposed signature to the Council on 11 Sep 2026 and that the deal was still 'concluded but not signed' in mid-Sep 2026. Sources conflict on whether it has been signed. Either way, CBAM continues to apply alongside the FTA.

Indian government activity: the Department of Commerce held an EU CBAM awareness session on 18 Aug 2026 for about 100 exporters, covering obligations, embedded-emissions calculation, data collection, verification, and steel and aluminium case studies (PIB PRID 2301032: https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2301032&reg=48&lang=1). On 27-29 Sep 2026, India reserved third-party rights in Russia's WTO dispute against EU CBAM (ET articleshow 134488568, 134548994). ET on 28 Sep 2026 reported 'India's bid to keep carbon cash home' via CCTS (articleshow 134531752).

MSME supply-chain pressure: ET (6-8 Sep 2026) reports that engineering goods exporters want the government to mandate accredited carbon-emission data from raw-material suppliers, and that about 70% of India's engineering exports to the EU come from MSMEs (ET articleshow 133830040). A Feb 2026 news digest says the Export Promotion Mission will partly fund compliance costs for rules such as CBAM. The digest gives the outlay as Rs 22,060 crore; that figure was not verified.

CCTS has no traded compliance price as of an Aug 2026 compilation, which weakens any EU Article 9 deduction today. The consolidated CBAM text lets the Commission set default carbon prices for third countries from 2027. Recitals to 2025/2083 limit deductions to carbon price 'effectively paid' and to actual (not default) values.

Steel exporters face a second barrier: the EU measure that replaced the steel safeguard has applied since 30 Jun 2026 (political agreement 14 Apr 2026). It tightens TRQs, adds country-specific quotas, and raises out-of-quota duties to up to 50%. A third-party JSW case study claims a 9.5% anti-dumping duty on Indian cold-rolled steel from 6 Aug 2026, but the EU trade-defence knowledge base mentions only expiry reviews (15 Sep 2026) of stainless cold-rolled measures on India. Treat the anti-dumping claim as unverified.

An illustrative third-party analysis of JSW cold-rolled exports uses BRSR FY2025-26 Scope 1 data (about 2.06 tCO2e/t crude steel), a 1.370 BF-BOF benchmark, the 97.5% factor and the EUR 75.36 Q1 price. It finds a 2026 CBAM cost of EUR 54.59/t with actual data against EUR 106.58/t with an illustrative default, a 48.8% saving. Its default assumption (2.5 + 10%) is lower than the India HRC default reported above (4.28), so the real gap may be larger. This is not an authoritative source.

PCF/EPD demand is driven mostly by buyers, because the regulatory triggers are deferred. CPR 2024/3110 GWP (EN 15804) declaration is indicative for 2029, pending a delegated act. The EU Battery Regulation carbon-footprint declaration is pending its delegated acts, though the battery passport is mandatory from 18 Feb 2027. No ESPR delegated act has been adopted for any product group, although the first ESPR working plan (16 Apr 2025) prioritises iron & steel and aluminium. White papers should not claim ISO 14067 is legally mandated for Indian exporters today.

Free 'India CBAM calculator' tools are multiplying, which signals that generic CBAM cost and calculator content is commoditising. GitHub repos created Jul-Sep 2026 include an SEE calculator with India defaults, an MSME PCF estimator, India-EU supplier carbon ratings, a CBAM+CCTS platform prototype and an LCA tool for Indian metals. Acquis Compliance also publishes an India CBAM cost dashboard, and a solo SaaS (BLARAA) claims CBAM+CCTS+RCO coverage.

ESG Astraa's own competitive research (unverified internal claims, no URLs in the doc) says: no product reconciles CCTS GEI (BEE method, financial year, gate-to-gate) with CBAM embedded emissions (EU method, calendar year, includes precursors). It also claims: Indian unwrought aluminium exports to the EU fell 41.7% year on year to Jan 2026; GTRI estimates 15-22% price cuts; more than EUR 6bn of Indian exports are CBAM-covered; Indian verifiers gained EU CBAM registry access in Sep 2026; and 255 iron & steel units were in a June 2026 CCTS draft. Re-source every figure before publishing.

key_findings.finding: METHOD NOTE (read first): WebSearch returned 'budget exhausted (200/200)' on the first call. Firecrawl search and scrape returned 402 (insufficient credits). The egress proxy blocked WebFetch to every regulator and standard-setter host tried: ifrs.org, efrag.org, eur-lex, consilium, sebi.gov.in, icai.org, globalreporting.org, sciencebasedtargets.org, ghgprotocol.org, cdp.net, plus search engines and Wikipedia. Only GitHub was reachable. So discovery used about 52 GitHub code searches, and facts come from (a) GitHub-hosted mirrors, scrapes and articles that quote primary sources with dates, and (b) primary datasets mirrored on GitHub (the GHG Protocol Scope 2 raw feedback file; GRI standard texts). Primary-source URLs named below were taken from those documents; I did not open them myself. To fix: add Firecrawl credits, raise CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_WEB_SEARCHES_PER_SESSION, or allow the hosts above in the environment's network settings. No search volumes were measured.

CSRD Omnibus I is now law. Directive (EU) 2026/470 was published in the Official Journal on 26 Feb 2026 and entered into force on 18 Mar 2026. Mandatory CSRD now applies only to undertakings or groups with more than 1,000 employees (average) AND more than EUR 450m net turnover, for financial years starting on or after 1 Jan 2027. Listed SMEs are removed from scope. Member States must transpose by 19 Mar 2027. The Council signed off on 24 Feb 2026. Several independent secondary sources agree: syntropyearth Sep 2026; firatbarca; brussels-governance-monitor; DreamLab knowledge graph.

Non-EU (third-country) parent test under 2026/470: EU net turnover above EUR 450m (previously EUR 150m) AND an EU subsidiary or branch above EUR 200m. The first reporting year is financial years starting on or after 1 Jan 2028. The separate standard for non-EU groups (NESRS) is still out for consultation, with EFRAG technical advice due by end-January 2027. This is the provision that reaches Indian groups with EU subsidiaries. Separately, an EU subsidiary that itself exceeds 1,000 employees and EUR 450m reports from FY2027.

Value-chain cap: undertakings with up to 1,000 employees can decline CSRD data requests that go beyond the voluntary (VSME-based) standard. The cap does NOT protect subsidiaries inside the reporting group's consolidation boundary, so Indian subsidiaries of EU groups still get full intragroup data requests.
key_findings.recency: 2026 (post-Directive 2026/470); corroborated by the syntropyearth article of 2026-09-24

key_findings.finding: Revised (simplified) ESRS: the Commission adopted the delegated act and the voluntary standard on 3 Jul 2026. They apply to financial years from 1 Jan 2027, and FY2026 early use is allowed once the act enters into force. Mandatory datapoints fall by about 61% (roughly 1,073 to roughly 320, per secondary sources). Reasonable assurance is dropped; limited assurance remains. EFRAG's Knowledge Hub was updated with the 2026 text (reported by IAS Plus, 29 Jul 2026). The 'Stop-the-clock' Directive (EU) 2025/794 had earlier postponed waves 2 and 3 by two years.
key_findings.recency: 2026-07-03 adoption; IAS Plus feed 2026-07-29 (https://github.com/pauliusgin/curated-news/blob/20cf26e81bfd2b6e0b80ab3b03d8ab42b839e14f/testdata/feeds/ias-plus.json). The 61% figure comes from https://github.com/DreamLab-AI/knowledgeGraph (secondary).

key_findings.finding: CSDDD after 2026/470 covers EU companies with more than 5,000 employees and more than EUR 1.5bn worldwide turnover, and non-EU companies with at least EUR 1.5bn EU turnover. Transposition is due 26 Jul 2028 and application starts 26 Jul 2029. For Indian suppliers, direct due-diligence pressure is therefore deferred and limited to very large buyers.

The ISSB issued 'Amendments to Greenhouse Gas Emissions Disclosures' (IFRS S2) in December 2025, effective for annual periods starting on or after 1 Jan 2027, with early application allowed. The main changes are relief letting financial institutions limit Category 15 to financed emissions and exclude derivatives, plus GHG Protocol and GWP measurement relief. In July 2026 the ISSB proposed a matching Sustainability Disclosure Taxonomy update, with comments due 28 Sep 2026.

India has NOT adopted ISSB standards, as far as accessible evidence shows. A 2026 country-by-country disclosure map lists India's regime as SEBI BRSR (mandatory for the top 1,000 listed companies since FY2022-23) plus BRSR Core, with no ISSB adoption. ICAI's CA Final study material for May 2027 teaches IFRS S1/S2 but names no Indian roadmap. ICAI's SSAE 3000 is the assurance standard used for BRSR Core. I could NOT verify any SEBI, MCA or ICAI ISSB-convergence decision, because sebi.gov.in and icai.org were blocked. Treat this as 'no evidence found', not a confirmed absence.

APAC peers are moving to ISSB-based mandates:
- Japan: FSA rules promulgated 20 Feb 2026 require SSBJ standards for Prime companies with 5-year average market cap of JPY 3tn or more from FY ending March 2027, and JPY 1tn or more from March 2028.
- Korea: FSC final plan of 8 Jul 2026 makes KSSB disclosure mandatory in 2028 (FY2027) for KOSPI firms with KRW 10tn+ assets; Scope 3 deferred 3 years; assurance from 2030.
- Malaysia: climate-first reporting from 2025/2026/2027 by group.
- Pakistan: SECP phase I from 1 Jul 2025.
- Sri Lanka: SLFRS S1/S2 mandatory for the top 100 from 2025.
- Taiwan: from FY2026.
- China: MoF Basic Standard (Nov 2024).

GRI changes, confirmed from the standards' own text:
- GRI 101: Biodiversity 2024 has been effective since 1 Jan 2026.
- GRI 102: Climate Change 2025 and GRI 103: Energy 2025 are effective for reports published on or after 1 Jan 2027. They supersede GRI 305-1 to 305-5 and GRI 302.

For Indian FY2026-27 reports, published around mid-2027, the reporting year already under way is covered.

key_findings.finding:
SBTi Corporate Net-Zero Standard V2.0 is published (by June 2026; translations dated Jul-Aug 2026).
- Transition: use V1.3.1 for 2026 submissions; either version from Q1 2027; V2 mandatory for submissions after 31 Jan 2028.
- Category A covers large companies everywhere plus medium companies in high-income countries. It requires near-term Scope 3 targets, transition-plan disclosure and limited assurance of base-year GHG data.
- Category B covers small companies everywhere plus medium companies in lower-income countries, with more flexibility.
- Category A removals obligation (Ongoing Emissions Responsibility) starts 2035.
- Scope 2 targets can be absolute or share of low-carbon electricity.
For Indian mid-caps, country income level may decide the category. (India is lower-middle income per the World Bank; this is model knowledge, not re-verified in this session.)

key_findings.finding:
GHG Protocol Scope 2 revision:
- The public consultation ran Oct 2025 to Jan 2026 and proposed hourly matching, deliverability and residual-mix reform.
- The GHG Protocol published the raw feedback on 29 Jul 2026: 1,072 respondents.
- My analysis of the published file: 70% of 909 respondents rated mandatory hourly matching 1-2 (oppose) and 22% rated it 4-5; among US respondents 78% opposed; 76% of 748 supported exemptions.
- India had only 12 respondents (Japan 80, China 65, Singapore 23). Indian respondents (n=10) averaged 2.7 on hourly matching against 1.77 for US respondents; 89% of 9 Indian respondents backed exemptions.
- CSEP (New Delhi) argued that India's integrated, nationally balanced grid dispatch should shape deliverability rules.
key_findings.recency: 2026-07-29 data. Processed mirror: https://github.com/jessicacohen554-cyber/scope-2-consult. Statistics computed by me in this session, with small Indian n.

key_findings.finding: GHG Protocol and ISO will combine their corporate carbon-accounting standards into a single harmonised global standard (announced July 2026). The same announcement reported Scope 2 consultation results and early feedback on the Actions and Market Instruments RFI. An integrated public consultation on the future corporate standard is planned for Q2 2027. The Scope 3 progress update of March 2026 includes draft requirements to disaggregate reported emissions by data type. Final standards were earlier expected in late 2027, with a 2-3 year phase-in.
