key_findings.finding: THEME RANKING (my judgement: timing x demand proxy x fit with ESG Astraa). 1) ESG data governance, assurance-readiness and human-approved AI: deadlines now (BRSR Core for the top 1,000 from FY2026-27; ISSA 5000 from 15 Dec 2026). 2) Anti-greenwashing and claim substantiation: EU EmpCo has applied since 27 Sep 2026; India CCPA guidelines from Oct 2024. 3) Internal carbon pricing derived from CBAM and CCTS: CBAM certificate sales start Feb 2027; the theme fits the CBAM/CCTS store best. 4) Renewable procurement and market-based Scope 2: GHG Protocol consultation results came out Jul 2026; the RCO trajectory runs to FY2029-30. 5) Physical risk at plant level (heat plus water): seasonal peak Mar-Jun. 6) Social data and just transition: Labour Codes since 21 Nov 2025; EU CSDDD applies from 2029. 7) Circularity and EPR: high compliance demand but a weaker platform fit. 8) AI's own footprint: niche. 9) Nature/TNFD: watch item; ISSB nature exposure draft targeted for CBD COP17 (Oct 2026), low uptake in India so far. Proxies: regulatory event dates below, BRSR mention prevalence, and counts of 2026 government releases. None of this is search volume.

BRSR corpus proxy (my analysis of public BRSR text files; FY2023-24 n=779, FY2024-25 n=700; share of filings mentioning a term). BRSR Core: 19.1% to 30.6%. 'Reasonable assurance': 20.7% to 28.1%. AI ('artificial intelligence' or 'AI'): 15.1% to 20.7%. Greenwashing: 3 to 11 filings (0.4% to 1.6%). Internal carbon price: 2 to 5 filings (0.3% to 0.7%; FY24-25 filers are Apollo Tyres, GHCL, Godrej Properties, Harsha Engineers and Himadri Speciality Chemical). TNFD: 6 to 8 filings (1.1%; includes Adani Power, Hindustan Zinc, Vedanta, TVS Motor, Tata Consumer, Suzlon, Huhtamaki India). Physical climate risk: 5.3% to 7.0%. Heat stress or heatwave: 4.5% to 5.1%. Climate scenario analysis: 1.2% to 1.9%. Market-based Scope 2: 6 to 12 filings (1.7%). REC or I-REC: 2.1%. Open access: 5.1%. PPA or captive: 8.1% to 10.6%. CCTS: 2 to 7. Just transition: 1 to 4. Caveat: the corpus is not a complete census of the top 1,000. Terms that appear in the BRSR template itself (EPR, water stress, Scope 3, human-rights due diligence, green credits) inflate raw mention counts, so those were not read as disclosure rates.
key_findings.recency: FY2023-24 and FY2024-25 filings (corpus commit Feb 2026)

key_findings.finding: Answer-level heuristic on the same corpus (rough, directional only). Among filings where the Scope 3 leadership-indicator answer could be classified, those reporting a numeric Scope 3 figure rose from 52% (187/357) in FY23-24 to 61% (207/342) in FY24-25. The rest said not applicable, not monitored or not calculated. For facilities in water-stress areas, about half of classifiable FY24-25 filings gave data (185/368); the other half said not applicable or none. Many filings could not be parsed, so treat these as directional numbers to motivate a rigorous proprietary study, not as publishable statistics.

SEBI circular of 28 Mar 2025 (SEBI/HO/CFD/CFD-PoD-1/P/CIR/2025/42) did four things. It let BRSR Core be checked by either 'assessment or assurance'. It made value-chain disclosure voluntary from FY2025-26, with its assessment or assurance from FY2026-27. It phased Core assurance by size. It added a voluntary green-credit leadership indicator from FY2024-25. Both circulars were later folded into SEBI's LODR master circular of 30 Jan 2026. The primary PDF is cited in the GitHub source as https://www.sebi.gov.in/sebi_data/attachdocs/mar-2025/1743159419610.pdf; it was not opened directly because of the egress block.

Master-circular consolidation of 30 Jan 2026 (covering circulars up to 30 Dec 2025, superseding the Nov 2024 version) is described in an explainer that also restates the assessment-or-assurance change and the value-chain deferral.

ISSA 5000 (IAASB) applies to sustainability assurance engagements for periods beginning on or after 15 Dec 2026 and replaces ISAE 3000/3410 use for sustainability. It requires assurers to evaluate the reliability of information used as evidence and to understand internal controls, even in limited-assurance engagements. Both GitHub sources are secondary; iaasb.org was blocked. India's ICAI has its own SSAE 3000, which appears as the governing standard in BRSR assurance contexts.
The EY CSRD barometer (May 2025) independently confirms the ISSA 5000 effective date: reporting periods starting on or after 15 Dec 2026.

EU anti-greenwashing status. Directive (EU) 2024/825 (EmpCo) had a transposition deadline of 27 Mar 2026 and member states must apply it from 27 Sep 2026. It bans generic environmental claims without recognised excellent performance, product-level neutrality claims based on offsets, self-made sustainability labels, and future-performance claims without detailed plans and independent verification. The Commission withdrew the separate Green Claims Directive proposal (COM(2023)166) in June 2025; the withdrawal intent was announced 20 Jun 2025. Footnoted primaries: eur-lex Directive 2024/825 and EESC 'Withdrawal of the Green Claims Directive' (Sep 2025).

UK: under the DMCC Act 2024 the CMA has had direct consumer enforcement powers since April 2025, with penalties of up to 10% of worldwide turnover. In 2026 the CMA issued 'Making green claims: getting it right across the supply chain', which says manufacturers, brands, distributors and retailers can be responsible for claims they originate or repeat. This matters to Indian suppliers whose data feeds UK buyers' claims.

India: the Central Consumer Protection Authority issued 'Guidelines for Prevention and Regulation of Greenwashing or Misleading Environmental Claims, 2024' dated 15 Oct 2024. This is evidenced by ASCI's advisories page as captured in a 25 Aug 2026 audit. The final text's detailed provisions were NOT re-verified here; consumeraffairs.nic.in and ascionline.in were blocked. ASCI's own green-claims guidelines could not be verified in this session.

SEBI anti-'purpose-washing' in capital markets. The ESG Debt Securities framework (circular of 5 Jun 2025) covers social, sustainability and sustainability-linked bonds and requires independent reviewers. On 27 Feb 2026 SEBI revised the reviewer/certifier norms for green debt securities to harmonise them with the other ESG debt types.

Under Omnibus I, the EU CSDDD now applies to companies with more than 5,000 employees and more than EUR 1.5bn turnover. Transposition is due by 26 Jul 2028 and compliance by 26 Jul 2029. The CSRD Omnibus (Directive (EU) 2026/470, OJ 26 Feb 2026, in force 18 Mar 2026) set CSRD thresholds at more than 1,000 employees and more than EUR 450m turnover.

CSRD Omnibus publication details (Directive (EU) 2026/470, 26 Feb 2026; revised ESRS due about Sep 2026) come from a May 2026 fact-currency sweep. That sweep cites Gibson Dunn and Covington; their pages were not opened. The same sweep says SBTi Corporate Net-Zero Standard V2 was not yet final as of May 2026 and becomes mandatory for new targets from 1 Jan 2028. It also gives a Q1 2026 CBAM certificate price of EUR 75.36.

Jul 2026 EU and standard-setter updates, read from an IAS Plus feed snapshot. The Commission adopted revised ESRSs and a voluntary standard for undertakings protected by the 'value chain cap' (delegated regulation of 3 Jul 2026); the revised ESRSs take effect 1 Jan 2027. EFRAG published an exposure draft on ESRS for certain non-EU undertakings (Art 40a) on 23 Jul 2026. GHG Protocol and ISO will merge their corporate standards into one harmonised standard and published Scope 2 consultation results plus Actions and Market Instruments (AMI) feedback (primary: ghgprotocol.org/blog/ghg-protocol-announces-key-standard-development-updates).

GHG Protocol Scope 2 revision. Public consultation ran Oct 2025 to Jan 2026 and proposed hourly matching and deliverability for market-based accounting; the final standard is expected around 2027. The GitHub source cites ghgprotocol.org/blog/upcoming-scope-2-public-consultation-hourly-matching-and-deliverability.

India renewable consumption obligation: the Ministry of Power has notified the RPO-then-RCO trajectory up to 2029-30. It applies to all designated consumers under the Energy Conservation Act 2001, carries penalties for non-compliance, and includes a decentralised-RE quantum (PIB, 16 Mar 2026).
key_findings.recency: 16 Mar 2026 (PIB text read via GitHub mirror)

key_findings.finding: RCO targets rise from 29.91% (FY2024-25) to 43.33% (FY2029-30) under the revised MoP framework (notified about 27 Sep 2025). CERC issued Virtual PPA guidelines on 24 Dec 2025 that let designated consumers meet RCO through VPPAs and RECs. Source is a secondary policy tracker citing beeindia.gov.in; the primary was not opened.

Under CCTS, obligated entities must disclose Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions (Ministry of Textiles Lok Sabha reply, 10 Mar 2026). The same reply cites the Eco-Mark Scheme 2024, which covers textiles, and a pilot on Product Environmental Footprint for SMEs.

India's NDC for 2031-35 was approved by Cabinet on 25 Mar 2026: a 47% cut in emissions intensity of GDP by 2035 from 2005, 60% non-fossil installed power capacity by 2035, and a 3.5-4.0 GtCO2e forest and tree carbon sink. Non-fossil capacity was already 52.57% in Feb 2026. The NDC also has an expanded adaptation section.

Heat as a 2026 workplace issue. The Ministry of Labour & Employment issued a nationwide heatwave advisory around 28 Apr 2026 asking States/UTs to direct employers to reschedule hours, provide water, rest and cooling, and have factory and mine managements slow work pace; fortnightly status reports were requested. The NHRC wrote to 21 states and Delhi citing NCRB data of 3,712 heat or sunstroke deaths in 2019-23 (PIB 2256123). IMD issued heatwave guidance on 25 Apr 2026 (PIB 2255487).

Water. At the World Water Day Conclave on 23 Mar 2026 (theme 'Industry for Water') the government released the National Water Data Policy 2026 and a Compendium of Good Practices on Industrial Water Use Efficiency. A 6 Aug 2026 Rajya Sabha reply on AI data centres said water availability in water-stressed regions is weighed in Environmental Clearance appraisal. It also said groundwater extraction is regulated under MoJS notification S.O. 3289(E) of 24 Sep 2020, as amended 29 Mar 2023 (PIB 2295675).

India's EPR regimes as listed in a 24 Mar 2026 Lok Sabha reply: waste tyres (2022); Battery Waste Management Rules 2022 (amended 2023 and 2024); E-Waste Rules 2022 (amended 2023); Plastic Waste Management Rules (amended Apr 2023); used oil (Sep 2023); End-of-Life Vehicles (6 Jan 2025); Construction and Demolition Waste (2 Apr 2025); non-ferrous metal scrap (1 Jul 2025). The rules impose annual recycling and recycled-content targets. NITI Aayog published three circularity reports in Jan 2026, and a Rs 1,500 crore critical-mineral recycling scheme exists. Solid Waste Management Rules 2026 are being rolled out (IEC campaign, PIB 2267715, 1 Jun 2026).

Trade link. On 31 Jul 2026 the Department of Commerce held a Trade and Sustainable Development workshop that tied CCTS, the Indian Carbon Market and the EPR framework to preparing for 'sustainability-related trade disciplines' (carbon border measures, standards) in FTAs. This makes circularity and carbon data an export-competitiveness topic.

Social dimension of ESG. India's four Labour Codes took effect on 21 Nov 2025. At an IICA/ILO inter-ministerial consultation in Mar 2026, MoLE flagged changes on minimum wages, appointment letters and social-security coverage, including ESIC applying pan-India and to hazardous industries regardless of size. Participants proposed integrating labour data from PLFS, ESIC and EPFO with SEBI's BRSR framework (PIB 2240319). At NCRBC in Jul 2026 a SEBI CGM said BRSR must evolve as sector-specific materiality and data gaps emerge (PIB 2286148).
Labour Codes effective date of 21 Nov 2025 is corroborated by an HR compliance source that cites PIB and Ministry of Labour releases.

AI governance in India. MeitY constituted the AI Governance and Economic Group (AIGEG) on 17 Apr 2026 to give effect to India's AI Governance Guidelines, supported by a Technology and Policy Expert Committee (PIB 2253322). An India AI Impact Summit working group on 'Resilience, Innovation & Efficiency' is examining energy, water and environmental resilience of AI infrastructure (PIB 2295675).

AI footprint baseline: the IEA 'Energy and AI' report (Apr 2025) puts data-centre electricity at about 415 TWh in 2024 (about 1.5% of global demand), projected to about 945 TWh by 2030 in the Base Case. The GitHub source quotes iea.org/reports/energy-and-ai, which was blocked here.

Global competitors are turning AI governance into a trust signal. Persefoni announced ISO/IEC 42001 (AI management system) certification on 24 Aug 2026 and published 'AI in Carbon Accounting [+ What to Ask Your Vendor]' (Nov 2025). Watershed launched AI features on 24 Jun 2026. No India-specific equivalent from Indian ESG vendors was checked or found in this session.

key_findings.finding: Nature. The ISSB plans a nature-related disclosures exposure draft by about Oct 2026, ahead of CBD COP17 (Yerevan, 19-30 Oct 2026). TNFD signed an MoU with the IFRS Foundation in Nov 2025 and is completing its technical work by Q3 2026. Whether the exposure draft has been published as of 1 Oct 2026 could NOT be verified (ifrs.org was blocked).
CBD COP17 dates confirmed as 19-30 Oct 2026 in Yerevan, Armenia, from GBIF's Data to Action Pavilion page.

Nature in India in practice. Tata Steel keeps a dedicated TNFD reports page that was updated in Jun 2026 (document-monitor diff). The GHG Protocol Land Sector and Removals Standard was finalised with a 1 Jan 2027 effective date (Watershed blog, 2 Jun 2026), which affects agri-linked and land-intensive supply chains.

Physical-risk regulation for lenders: the RBI's 'Draft Disclosure Framework on Climate-related Financial Risks' (Feb 2024) covers governance, strategy, risk management and metrics, and the RBI launched RB-CRIS, a climate risk data portal. Final issuance status as of Oct 2026 could NOT be verified; rbi.org.in was blocked and no GitHub source showed a final circular.

India's Department of Economic Affairs invited comments on a Draft Framework of 'India's Climate Finance Taxonomy' by 25 Jun 2025 (PIB 2127562, 7 May 2025). Whether a final taxonomy was issued was not verified. A taxonomy matters for green-claim credibility in lending and bonds.

Proxy for government attention: counts of 2026 releases mentioning each theme, from a UPSC-filtered PIB subset (7,483 releases, 25 Feb to 1 Oct 2026). Water conservation/groundwater 219; biodiversity 198; AI with energy, water or data centres 129; EPR/circular economy 127; heat/heatwave 40; Labour Codes 35; BRSR, responsible business or ESG 26; open access/RCO/REC 17; carbon market/CCTS 11; CBAM 8; greenwashing 0. This measures how much the government communicates on each theme, not search demand. It suggests water, circularity and heat are policy-salient while greenwashing is driven by regulation rather than news in India.

Not verified because of access limits: whether trading of Carbon Credit Certificates has started on power exchanges; final RBI climate disclosure directions; ASCI green-claims guideline text; the CCPA guideline provisions in detail; India's final climate finance taxonomy; publication of the ISSB nature exposure draft; EU EmpCo transposition status by member state; plastic EPR target percentages for FY2025-26 and later (a secondary source cites 60% for 2024-25 and 80% for 2026-27 recycling; not used).

key_findings.finding: ACCESS LIMITS (read first). WebSearch had already used its 200-call session budget when this researcher started; all 3 WebSearch calls returned 'budget exhausted'. Firecrawl returned 402 (low credits). The egress proxy blocked WebFetch and curl to nseindia.com, bseindia.com, sebi.gov.in, mca.gov.in, pib.gov.in, developers.google.com, arxiv.org, contentmarketinginstitute.com, ahrefs.com, edelman.com, schema.org and more; only GitHub and package registries were reachable. Evidence therefore comes from (a) GitHub code search (21 queries) and (b) public GitHub repos that hold primary data (BRSR XBRL manifests, the SEBI taxonomy, Gazette PDFs, EU CBAM default values) or verbatim captures of primary pages. Where only a secondary capture was available, the finding says so and its confidence is lowered. No search volumes or backlink counts were measured.

BRSR filings ARE machine-readable XBRL on NSE and BSE. NSE's BRSR page is a React app backed by the JSON endpoint /api/corporate-bussiness-sustainabilitiy (NSE's own spelling). Each row gives company, symbol, financial-year range, submission and revision dates, a PDF URL (attachmentFile) and an XBRL URL (xbrlFile). Files are hosted at nsearchives.nseindia.com/corporate/xbrl/. BSE serves the same filings at bseindia.com/XBRLFILES/BRSRUploadDocument/BRSR_<scrip>_<timestamp>.xml, plus a PDF. A public manifest dated 2 Jul 2026 shows FY2025-26 BRSR XBRL already filed: TCS on BSE 15 May 2026, Reliance on BSE 28 May 2026 (NSE copy 6 Jun 2026). The legal basis cited in that code is LODR Reg 34(2)(f). MCA: no evidence found that BRSR is filed in XBRL on MCA21, and mca.gov.in was blocked, so treat MCA as NOT verified. Practical note: NSE returns 403 without session cookies and a Referer header (no login needed). One open-source team keeps automated NSE access behind a 'fail-closed' legal approval gate at 0.5 requests/second, so review exchange terms of use before bulk collection.

The SEBI BRSR XBRL taxonomy can support quantitative benchmarks. The core schema (in-capmkt.xsd) has about 2,600 named element definitions, including:
- TotalScope1Emissions, TotalScope2Emissions, TotalScope3Emissions
- TotalScope1AndScope2EmissionsIntensityPerRupeeOfTurnoverAdjustedForPurchasingPowerParity (the BRSR Core metric)
- the name of the external assurance or assessment agency for GHG and for Scope 3
- per-disclosure 'AssuranceSubTypeFor…' elements and an AssessmentOrAssuranceProviderAxis
- value-chain elements (e.g. % of value-chain partners assessed; green credits of the top-ten value-chain partners)
Taxonomy versions seen: 2021-09-30, 2024-04-30 and 2025-05-31. A parser test fixture for an FY2025-26 filing (1 Apr 2025 to 31 Mar 2026) uses a namespace dated 2026-02-28. A filing-level assurance tracker, a GHG-intensity benchmark and a Scope 3 disclosure study can therefore be built without PDF scraping.

Proof that a top-1000 BRSR dataset is feasible, and that a data-quality layer is essential. One open project parsed FY2024-25 BRSR XBRL for the NIFTY 100 (state as of 16 Aug 2026):
- 93 filings parsed and 204,880 raw XBRL facts
- 7 companies with no FY25 BRSR under their NSE symbol (e.g. ABB, Siemens; calendar-year filers or demerged entities)
- 16 values withheld: 7 ambiguous turnover scales, and 9 energy facts filed under a bare 'J' unit at inconsistent magnitudes (TVS Motor 676,660 vs Jindal Steel 239.51)
A second project (as of 27 Jul 2026) found 413 companies with BRSRs for all of FY2023-24, FY2024-25 and FY2025-26 on NSE, and 870 companies with partial history. Implication: any ESG Astraa benchmark must publish its cohort rules, unit normalisation and withheld-value counts. Those method notes are themselves citable content.

Illustrative pilot on public BRSR text extracts. A public GitHub corpus holds 821 FY2023-24 and 729 FY2024-25 BRSR PDF-to-text files; its provenance is undocumented, it is not the full top-1000, and the two years are not a matched panel. My own keyword scan found:
- 'CBAM' in 6 of 821 filings (0.7%) and 5 of 729 (0.7%)
- CCTS or Indian Carbon Market in 2 (0.2%) and 7 (1.0%)
- 'BRSR Core' in 149 (18.1%) and 214 (29.4%)
- 'reasonable assurance' in 161 (19.6%) and 198 (27.2%)
- Scope 3 in 68.1% and 71.6% (inflated, because the BRSR format itself asks about Scope 3)
These are directional only. They suggest clear hooks: a CBAM and CCTS disclosure gap among listed companies, and fast growth in BRSR Core assurance language. Re-run on exchange XBRL before publishing any figure.
key_findings.recency: FY2023-24 and FY2024-25 filings; scan run 2026-10-01

key_findings.finding:
Formats that work for AI citation: Google says no special AEO markup is needed, and original data is what gets cited. Google's 'AI features and your website' page (read via a verbatim mirror) says:
- 'There are no additional requirements to appear in AI Overviews or AI Mode'
- 'You don't need to create new machine readable files, AI text files, or markup… no special schema.org structured data'
Best practices it lists: crawlable pages, internal links, important content 'in textual form', and structured data that 'matches the visible text'. AI Mode uses 'query fan-out' across subtopics. Separately, the GEO paper (Aggarwal et al., arXiv 2311.09735) reports gains of 'up to 40%' in generative-engine visibility. The methods it tested include adding statistics, adding quotations and citing credible sources; per-method results could not be re-verified because arXiv was blocked. Playbook: publish every white paper as a full HTML report. Use one finding per H2/H3, a one-sentence answer-first summary, the exact statistic with its date and denominator, and tables in HTML rather than images. Treat the PDF as a companion file, not the primary artefact.
key_findings.recency: Google doc mirror read 2026-10-01; GEO repo https://github.com/GEO-optim/GEO

key_findings.finding: Recent AI-citation shifts favour primary-source research over listicles. Peec AI data, shared via Lily Ray in August 2026 (secondary; vendor data), says that after the ChatGPT 5.6 release, listicles fell from 15.77% to 7.80% of ChatGPT citations (-50.5%) and comparison/'vs' pages from 9.08% to 6.17% (-32.1%). Over the same period, 'site:' and 'official' searches rose. The source rates 'original research + data' as strong on ChatGPT, Google AIO, Gemini and Perplexity. Implication for ESG Astraa: competitors currently win Indian category SERPs with 'best BRSR/CBAM software 2026' listicles (per the brand research). An original-data white paper is the more durable AEO play than copying those listicles.

Gating: use a hybrid model. Put full findings in ungated HTML and gate only the data pack. Evidence:
- 6sense 2025 Buyer Experience Report (about 4,000 respondents, published 12 Nov 2025): 94% of buyers ranked their shortlist before engaging sellers; the preferred pre-contact vendor won 77% of the time; first seller contact came 61% of the way through the journey.
- G2 (company-stated, 8 Jan 2026), citing an August 2025 survey: 87% of B2B software buyers say AI chatbots have changed how they research, and half now start with an AI chatbot rather than Google.
- Gated pages and PDF-only content are not visible as crawlable text (Google guidance above).
Recommendation:
- Ungated: the HTML report, all headline statistics, charts and methodology.
- Gated (email): the company-level CSV/XLSX extract, sector cuts, and a 'benchmark your company' self-assessment. These produce identified leads without hiding the citable claims.
Both buyer surveys were read via GitHub-preserved captures; the primary URLs are 6sense.com/science-of-b2b/buyer-experience-report-2025/ and learn.g2.com/g2-traffic-momentum.

Who reads thought leadership matches ESG Astraa's buyers. Figures from the Edelman-LinkedIn 2025 B2B Thought Leadership Impact Report (secondary summary; the primary edelman.com page could not be opened):
- 71% of 'hidden decision-makers' (finance, legal, compliance, operations) say thought leadership shows vendor capability better than conventional marketing
- 64% trust it more than marketing materials
- 79% are more likely to support proposals from vendors who publish strong thought leadership
These hidden roles map directly to ESG Astraa's CFO and Company Secretary buyers, who own BRSR sign-off. White papers should therefore be written for finance and compliance readers: risk, cost, deadlines and audit evidence, not sustainability vision.

Making white papers rank needs a hub-and-spoke cluster plus technical hygiene:
- One canonical pillar page per report at a keyword slug (e.g. /research/brsr-core-assurance-tracker-2026), not the current numeric /insights/blogs/2 pattern.
- 6-10 spoke posts, one per finding or AEO question, each linking back to the pillar with descriptive anchors, and the pillar linking out to them.
- An FAQ block that answers the buyer questions verbatim.
- Article or Report JSON-LD (schema.org 'Report' is a subtype of Article, 'a Report generated by governmental or non-governmental organization') and Organization/author markup. Markup must match visible text and does not by itself win AI placement.
- A Dataset description for the downloadable data.
- The PDF with proper document title metadata and a plain filename (the current H&M PDF has no title metadata and an '&' in its name).
- Desk-research case studies labelled as such, to avoid AI misattribution.

Crawler access for AI citation. Allow the retrieval and search bots in robots.txt and CDN rules: OAI-SearchBot ('surface as results in SearchGPT'), ChatGPT-User, Claude-SearchBot, PerplexityBot, and Googlebot. Training bots (GPTBot, ClaudeBot) and Google-Extended can be decided separately; Google-Extended 'does not impact a site's inclusion or ranking in Google Search'. llms.txt v2 (Jeremy Howard, modified 10 Aug 2026) is widely adopted and recommends .md copies of key pages, but Google states no AI text files are needed. Treat llms.txt as a cheap optional extra listing the research hub, not a ranking lever.

Measurement: track AI visibility and impressions, not only clicks. Pew Research (July 2025; 68,879 Google searches by about 900 US adults in March 2025) found:
- users clicked a traditional result on 8% of visits when an AI summary appeared, vs 15% without
- links inside the summary got about 1% of clicks
First-party tools now exist:
- Google added generative AI performance reports to Search Console on 3 June 2026: impressions in AI Overviews, AI Mode and Discover; no clicks yet; UK rolled out first, so Indian properties may not see data yet.
- GA4's default channel group has an 'AI Assistant' channel (medium 'ai-assistant'; ChatGPT, Gemini, DeepSeek, Copilot, Grok). AI Overview and AI Mode clicks stay in Organic Search, and many assistant clicks arrive as Direct.
Recommended KPI stack per white paper:
1. AI share of voice: a fixed panel of about 50 buyer prompts across ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini and Google AI Mode, run monthly, logging mention and citation of esgastraa.com vs competitors.
2. Search Console AI and organic impressions for pillar and spokes.
3. GA4 AI-assistant and organic sessions.
4. Data-pack downloads leading to MQLs and SQLs.
5. Assisted pipeline: opportunities whose contacts viewed report pages before first meeting.
6. A self-reported 'How did you hear about us?' field with an AI-assistant option.
7. Referring domains and press citations.
8. Branded search growth for 'ESG Astraa', given the Astra ESG name collision.

Distribution: LinkedIn is the main channel and also an AI-citation surface.
- Semrush tracked the top 25 most-cited domains across ChatGPT Search, Google AI Mode and Perplexity for 13 weeks (230,000+ prompts, 100M+ citations). Reddit, Wikipedia, LinkedIn, YouTube and Google properties led, and no brand product sites made the list.
- LinkedIn's own AEO guidance, reported September 2026 (platform-reported), says LinkedIn is the most-cited outlet for professional topics, Articles produce about 60% of its citations vs about 40% for Posts, and a post's opening words become its URL slug.
- CMI 2024 (via Ahrefs' compilation): 85% of B2B marketers rate LinkedIn the best-performing social platform.
Playbook: publish each report's findings as founder-bylined LinkedIn Articles (not just posts) that link to the pillar; run a LinkedIn newsletter timed to filing and regulatory dates; seed one data chart per week.
Not verified online this session (sites blocked): Indian industry-body routes. Candidates are ICSI (company secretaries own BRSR), the ICAI Sustainability Reporting Standards Board, CII/FICCI sustainability councils, and EEPC India/FIEO for CBAM exporters. Also list on OneStopESG and Indian business-press data desks for earned citations.

Original research is under-used but tends to pay off (vendor surveys via Ahrefs' 105-statistics compilation, updated 22 Dec 2025):
- Orbit Media 2025: almost half of content programs now publish original research, and 25% of those report strong results; original research is among the most effective and least used tactics
- Datalily 2025: 86% of marketers plan to raise proprietary-research budgets in 2026; 64% report higher conversion from content-sourced leads since adopting proprietary research
- LinkedIn/Ipsos 2025 B2B Marketing Benchmark (1,500 senior B2B marketers): 94% say trust is important to B2B success
Treat all of these as vendor-sourced directional evidence, not causal proof.

Cadence anchored to the Indian compliance calendar:
- Annual flagship BRSR data report, published Sept-Oct after the May-August filing season. In the manifest above, FY2025-26 BRSRs landed 15 May to 6 Jun 2026, and Reliance's FY2024-25 BRSR on NSE on 7 Aug 2025.
- Annual CBAM report before the 1 Feb 2027 start of certificate sales and refreshed before the 30 Sep 2027 first declaration.
- CCTS update after each GEI-target Gazette notification.
- Quarterly 'regulatory pulse' refresh of each pillar with a visible 'last updated' date.
- 2-4 spoke posts a month.
One flagship plus three or four derivative white papers a year is realistic for a small team. The XBRL pipeline makes yearly refreshes cheap, and comparing years compounds the citation value.

Regulatory why-now (BRSR). SEBI circular CIR/2025/42 of 28 Mar 2025 phases BRSR Core 'assurance or assessment':
- top 150 from FY2023-24
- top 250 from FY2024-25
- top 500 from FY2025-26
- top 1,000 from FY2026-27
Value-chain disclosures are voluntary for the top 250 from FY2025-26, and their assurance is voluntary from FY2026-27. Only value-chain partners at 2% or more of purchases or sales count, with coverage capped at those making up 75% cumulatively. The circular also introduced voluntary green-credit disclosure. sebi.gov.in was blocked, so this was read via a May 2026 research note that cites the SEBI circular URLs (SEBI CIR/2025/42: https://www.sebi.gov.in/legal/circulars/mar-2025/measures-to-facilitate-ease-of-doing-business-with-respect-to-framework-for-assurance-or-assessment-esg-disclosures-for-value-chain-and-introduction-of-voluntary-disclosure-on-green-credits_93102.html). It matches the phase-in in the brand research.

Regulatory why-now (CBAM). The CBAM default values are in Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/2621, Annex I, as replaced by Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1740 (OJ L, 31 Jul 2026; adopted 20 Jul 2026; some aluminium values corrected retroactively to 1 Jan 2026). When defaults are used to count certificates, total-emission defaults are marked up as follows:
- cement, iron and steel, aluminium, hydrogen: 10% for 2026, 20% for 2027, 30% for 2028 onward
- fertilisers: 1%
Example, unwrought aluminium (CN 7601 10 00), before mark-up: India 1.870 tCO2e/t vs 'other countries' 2.203 vs the Annex IV 'origin unknown' 3.198. This was read from a tool's dated quotation of the consolidated EUR-Lex text and the Commission's default-value Excel (v2, 6 Aug 2026), retrieved 24 Sep 2026; EUR-Lex itself was blocked. Combined with the definitive period from 1 Jan 2026, certificate sales from 1 Feb 2027 and the first declaration by 30 Sep 2027 (EC sources in the brand research), this gives a precise 'cost of not measuring' storyline.

Regulatory why-now (CCTS), newer than the brand brief. On 26 June 2026, MoEFCC published DRAFT notification G.S.R. 517(E) (Gazette CG-DL-E-02072026-274012) proposing GHG emission intensity targets for the Iron & Steel sector. It covers 255 unique obligated-entity IDs (INSOE…), including SAIL plants, Tata Steel, JSW Steel, AM/NS and JSPL, with a 60-day objection window. Earlier notifications: G.S.R. 739(E) of 8 Oct 2025 (aluminium, cement, chlor-alkali, pulp & paper) and the 13 Jan 2026 notification (secondary aluminium, refineries, petrochemicals, textiles). A CC BY 4.0 open dataset, 'CCTS-745' (Zenodo DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21671592), standardises all 745 facilities across Phases I-III. Steel is both a CBAM good and now proposed for CCTS. Whether the steel draft has been finalised could NOT be verified.

key_findings.finding: METHOD AND ACCESS LIMITS (read first). The shared WebSearch budget was used up (200/200) before this researcher started, so all 4 WebSearch calls failed. Firecrawl returned HTTP 402 (no credits). The egress proxy blocked WebFetch to every regulator and news domain I tried: acra.gov.sg, sgx.com, sc.com.my, ifrs.org, moccae.gov.ae, cma.org.sa, ojk.go.id, gov.uk, eur-lex.europa.eu, pib.gov.in, wikipedia, pwc.com and lexology. Only GitHub could be reached. I therefore ran 37 GitHub code and repository searches, read public GitHub-hosted corpora that quote primary texts, and read a scraped PIB press-release dataset that another researcher had stored in the session scratchpad. No regulator page was opened directly; each finding below names the corpus it came from. Confidence is capped at medium where only a secondary source exists. No search volumes were measured.

UAE Federal Decree-Law No. 11 of 2024 on the Reduction of Climate Change Effects. It was issued 28 Aug 2024, published 30 Aug 2024, and entered into force 30 May 2025. Sources had one year to bring their status into line, so the default adjustment window closed on 30 May 2026. The Cabinet may extend it; law firms reported an extension was expected, but the corpus found no extension resolution. Article 6(1) requires designated sources to measure GHG emissions, keep an emissions inventory, submit periodic reports and reduction measures on Ministry forms, and keep records for 5 years. Article 15 sets fines of AED 50,000 to 2,000,000, and Article 16 doubles them for a repeat offence within 2 years. Article 17 administrative penalties await a Cabinet resolution. Source: a curated corpus quoting the official portal (https://uaelegislation.gov.ae/en/legislations/2558, not opened directly).

UAE Cabinet Resolution No. 67 of 2024 (National Register for Carbon Credits) has been in force since 28 Dec 2024. It is mandatory for entities emitting 0.5 MtCO2e or more per year across Scope 1+2. These entities must run IPCC-based MRV, file an annual GHG report, and have emission-reduction reports verified to ISO 14065. Annex 2 fines run from AED 500,000 to 2,000,000. Primary source cited by the corpus: https://uaelegislation.gov.ae/en/legislations/2521 (not opened).

Abu Dhabi facility-level MRV (EAD Technical Guidance v8, 27 Feb 2026) implements Article 6 of the Decree-Law. Scope: facilities in power and water, oil and gas, industry and transport that emit 25,000 tCO2e or more of Scope 1 a year. Only CO2 and CH4 count, the test is per facility, and the boundary is operational control; free zones are included. The annual report is due 31 March, with a grace period to 14 April per EAD's March 2026 workshop. Third-party verification (ISO 14065/17029) is not obligatory until 2027. Methane uses AR5 GWP of 28. Activity-data tiers mirror the EU ETS (±7.5%, ±5%, ±2.5%, ±1.5%), and the guidance sets de minimis and minor source-stream rules and a mandatory data-gap table. Primary PDFs cited by the corpus: https://facilitymrv.ead.ae/appDocuments/20260227%20-%20Technical%20Guidance%20v8.pdf and https://facilitymrv.ead.ae/appDocuments/20260312_EAD%20MRV_%20Workshop%20Presentation.pdf (not opened).

Unverified: a claim that the UAE SCA has mandated IFRS/ISSB sustainability standards for listed companies from 2025 appears only on a low-quality consultant blog. No regulator or law-firm source confirmed it. Treat UAE listed-company ISSB status as unverified.

Saudi Arabia: a policy tracker checked on 1 Aug 2026 lists the CMA/Tadawul sustainability disclosure regime as voluntary. Its entries are 'comply-or-explain' and 'recommends GRI/SASB-aligned disclosure'. The only mandatory item listed is the CMA green, social and sustainability-linked bond disclosure rules (2025), which apply to in-scope bond issuers only. The Saudi Exchange ESG Disclosure Guidelines PDF is at https://www.saudiexchange.sa/wps/wcm/connect/d0922cd6-e0bf-4554-ad4d-03f0c2eea5ad/ESG_Disclosure_Guidelines_EN.pdf (not opened). I found no evidence of a mandatory ISSB-based regime in Saudi Arabia as of Aug 2026.

Singapore tiered climate reporting:
- STI constituents report ISSB-aligned climate disclosures from FY2025, with Scope 3 from FY2026.
- Other listed issuers with market cap of S$1bn or more report from FY2028; the remaining listed issuers from FY2030.
- Large non-listed companies report from FY2030.
- Scope 3 stays voluntary outside the STI tier.
The dataset cites https://www.sgx.com/regulation/sustainability-reporting (blocked, not opened). A separate EY-competitor dataset independently gives the same STI FY2025 and Scope 3 FY2026 dates and says others were deferred to FY2028-2030.

Malaysia's NSRF uses IFRS S1/S2 with climate-first reporting:
- Group 1 (Main Market, market cap of RM2bn or more) from FY2025.
- Group 2 (other Main Market issuers) from FY2026.
- Group 3 (ACE Market plus non-listed companies with revenue of RM2bn or more) from FY2027.
- Full IFRS S1/S2 from 2027, 2028 and 2030 respectively.
Two independent secondary sources agree. Terrascope published a dedicated explainer on 11 Jun 2026. The dataset cites Bursa's 23 Dec 2024 media release and the IFRS jurisdiction profile (neither opened).

Malaysia's Simplified ESG Disclosure Guide (SEDG) for SMEs is voluntary. Version 2 aligns with the ASEAN Simplified ESG Disclosure Guide launched by the ASEAN Capital Markets Forum in April 2025. This is a ready-made supplier-data template that listed buyers push down to suppliers for Scope 3.

Indonesia: DSK IAI's PSPK 1 and PSPK 2 (IFRS S1/S2-aligned) take effect 1 Jan 2027 (Terrascope, 16 Jun 2026). OJK's draft ISSB-aligned mandate, an amendment to POJK 51/2017, ran a public consultation to 13 Mar 2026. As of Jul 2026 OJK was still drafting, aiming to publish before end-2026 with a 1 Jan 2027 effective date. Terrascope describes a phase-in from FY2027 to FY2029.

Sri Lanka: SLFRS S1/S2 (localised IFRS S1/S2) could be used voluntarily from 1 Jan 2024. They became mandatory from 1 Jan 2025 for the top 100 CSE-listed companies and broaden in 2026-2027. In July 2026 the Prime Minister referred to 'mandatory sustainability disclosure standards under SLFRS S1 and SLFRS S2 for leading listed companies', and CA Sri Lanka published a Preparers' Guide to SLFRS S1 & S2.

Bangladesh: a 5 Sep 2026 research note summarising FRC 2026 notifications says IFRS S1 and S2 are 'permitted', not mandated. A climate-disclosure map found only a Bangladesh Bank sustainability guideline for banks, with no jurisdiction-wide ISSB mandate. In practice, demand for supplier data comes from buyers, not from the domestic regulator.

Vietnam:
- Decree 06/2022/ND-CP set a carbon-market roadmap: pilot from 2025, full operation from 2028, with offsets capped at 10% of allowances.
- Decision 01/2022/QD-TTg obliged 1,912 facilities to do GHG inventories.
- Decision 232/QD-TTg (24 Jan 2025) approved the carbon-market scheme.
- Decree 119/2025/ND-CP makes the Ministry of Agriculture and Environment responsible for the national registry and national emission-factor database.
The updated obligated-facility list and pilot ETS allocation decrees could not be verified.

United Kingdom: UK SRS S1 and S2 were published 25 Feb 2026 and are voluntary today. The FCA proposes mandatory UK SRS S2 climate disclosure for about 515 listed companies in three listing categories, for periods beginning on or after 1 Jan 2027 (first reports in 2028), with comply-or-explain for Scope 3. Requirements for private companies are subject to a separate government consultation. This matters for UK subsidiaries of Indian groups, which today fall under SECR and the Companies Act climate disclosure rules if large.

UK CBAM starts 1 Jan 2027 and covers aluminium, cement, fertilisers, hydrogen, and iron & steel; glass and ceramics are excluded from the initial scope, per the UK government consultation response. Source: an EU Climate Advisory Board dataset marked 'AI-compiled, pending verification' that cites https://www.gov.uk/government/consultations/introduction-of-a-uk-carbon-border-adjustment-mechanism-from-january-2027 (blocked, not opened). Whether the primary legislation has passed could not be verified.

The India-UK CETA entered into force on 15 Jul 2026 (signed 24 Jul 2025). It gives zero-duty access on about 99% of tariff lines and removes UK tariffs of up to 12% on textiles and clothing and up to 18% on engineering goods. Separately, new UK steel measures on 188 tariff lines took effect 1 Jul 2026, covering about 14% (USD 137m) of India's steel exports to the UK. On 26 Jun 2026 the government announced it would deploy 1,000 advisory personnel to help businesses use the CETA (PRID 2278276).

The India-EU FTA was concluded at the India-EU Summit on 27 Jan 2026. It is not yet in force: on 22 Sep 2026 India was still seeking the European Parliament's 'early signing and ratification' (PRID 2313468). CBAM cooperation was on the agenda of the Commerce Minister's July 2026 EU visit (PRID 2286360). PIB lists the FTA as 'awaiting implementation', with preferential treatment across 97% of EU tariff lines (PRID 2300733).

The Department of Commerce, with NABCB and EEPC, ran an EU CBAM awareness session for about 100 exporters on 18 Aug 2026. It covered applicability, embedded-emissions calculation, data collection and accreditation/verification, which shows government-recognised demand for practical verification-ready CBAM guidance. The India-EFTA TEPA has been in force since 1 Oct 2025 (PRID 2254367).

CSRD after Omnibus I: Directive (EU) 2026/470 was published in the OJ on 26 Feb 2026 and has been in force since 18 Mar 2026.
- Scope: undertakings and groups above EUR 450m net turnover and an average of 1,000 employees.
- Non-EU groups: in scope if EU turnover exceeds EUR 450m (previously EUR 150m) and an EU subsidiary or branch exceeds EUR 200m, for financial years beginning on or after 1 Jan 2028.
- Value-chain cap: 'protected undertakings' with 1,000 or fewer employees may decline requests beyond the voluntary standard.
- Transposition deadline: 19 Mar 2027.
Read from an article based on the directive text; EUR-Lex (https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2026/470/oj) was blocked.

The Commission adopted the revised, simplified ESRS as delegated acts on 3 Jul 2026, with about 61% fewer mandatory datapoints, applying from FY2027 and in Parliament/Council scrutiny at the time. The voluntary VSME standard was adopted the same day; it is the reference for what suppliers outside CSRD scope can be asked for.

CSDDD thresholds after Omnibus conflict across the secondary sources I found. One says more than 5,000 employees and EUR 1.5bn turnover, with application 26 Jul 2029. Another says more than 1,000 employees and EUR 450m. This was not verified, and no CSDDD figure should be published without checking EUR-Lex.

EU ESPR (Reg (EU) 2024/1781): from 19 Jul 2026, large companies (250+ staff and more than EUR 50m) may not destroy unsold apparel, clothing accessories and footwear. Medium-sized companies follow from 19 Jul 2030. Article 24 requires annual disclosure of discarded unsold products by category and reason, with a standard format under Implementing Reg (EU) 2026/2 that applies from 2 Mar 2027. This pushes traceability and product-data demands onto garment suppliers.

Buyer pressure on garment and textile suppliers, as shown in brands' own 2024-25 reports:
- Lululemon targets 25% renewable electricity among core Tier 1 and Tier 2 suppliers (more than 75% of production volume) for its SBTi Scope 3 target.
- Puma reports that of 23 factories approached, 13 submitted data and only 6 could be validated because 7 lacked supporting documents.
Supplier data with an evidence trail is the bottleneck.

India-UAE bilateral merchandise trade crossed US$100bn for the first time, reaching US$101.25bn in FY2025-26. Both governments target US$200bn by 2032. Cumulative UAE FDI into India was US$25.19bn (April 2000 to March 2025). India's textile exports grew 2.1% in FY2025-26 (PRID 2254367).

Data hook I computed: a regex scan of a public GitHub corpus of 729 FY2024-25 BRSR text files found:
- CBAM in 5 filings (0.7%), CSRD/ESRS in 10 (1.4%), ISSB/IFRS S1-S2 in 20 (2.7%), and UK SRS or SECR in 0.
- 201 filings (28%) place 'subsidiar*' within 200 characters of a foreign geography: UAE 78, Singapore 82, UK 68, EU countries 60, Bangladesh/Sri Lanka/Vietnam 31, Saudi 8.
- 73 filings (10%) mention UAE/Dubai/Abu Dhabi anywhere.
- FY2023-24 (821 files): CBAM 6 (0.7%), CSRD 6 (0.7%), ISSB 15 (1.8%).
The proximity test is crude and includes false positives, the corpus is not the full top-1,000, and the counts need manual validation before publication.

Competitor coverage of international markets. Terrascope, Singapore-based and acquired Feb 2026, runs a 'Climate Disclosure Rules: What You Need to Know' series: Hong Kong (5 Jun 2026), Malaysia and New Zealand (11 Jun), Australia and Indonesia (16 Jun), Switzerland (15 Sep) and UK (16 Sep). Persefoni covers Singapore (22 Dec 2025), Japan, Korea, Mexico, Canada and Australia, plus an EU CBAM explainer (30 Jan 2026). Neither feed (Terrascope 45 posts, Persefoni 95 posts) has a post on the UAE climate law, Saudi Arabia, Vietnam, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka or India's BRSR/CCTS. I checked only these mirrored feeds; Big 4 and law-firm content could not be checked.

Ranking pages are moving to comparison and selection formats: Terrascope published 'Spreadsheet, consultancy, software or Terrascope' (28 Aug 2026) and 'The 10 best carbon management platforms for enterprise' (17 Sep 2026); Persefoni published several 'best ... software in 2026' listicles. Multi-jurisdiction comparison tables are the format competitors are betting on.

METHOD LIMITS (read first). I could not spot-check live search results in this run:
- WebSearch refused every query because the session's budget was used up (200 of 200 calls).
- Firecrawl search returned HTTP 402 (out of credits).
- The egress proxy blocked every search engine (Google, Bing, DuckDuckGo, Yahoo, Startpage, Ecosia, Qwant, Yandex, Mojeek, Marginalia, Google Trends), Wikimedia pageviews, and the competitor and regulator sites I tried (thesustainabilitycloud.com and climate-decode.com via WebFetch; sebi.gov.in, pib.gov.in and economictimes.indiatimes.com via curl).
- Only github.com and raw.githubusercontent.com were reachable.

No search volumes, keyword difficulty or SERP features were observed, and none are claimed. Every demand and difficulty statement above is an estimate.

The candidates I am least sure about, and which need a live SERP check first once access returns, are C04, C05, C09, C12, C17, C18, C21, C22, C24, C28, C31 and C45. To unblock: raise CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_WEB_SEARCHES_PER_SESSION, add Firecrawl credits, or allow google.com/bing.com in the environment's Network access settings.

PROXIES USED INSTEAD:
(1) Category SERPs captured earlier in this session by the brand pass (BRSR software, CBAM software, CCTS software, India carbon accounting).
(2) News cadence from a GitHub-archived Economic Times/Moneycontrol digest (https://github.com/abhishekfolder-spec/my-news), 66 daily files from 27 Jul to 1 Oct 2026:
- CBAM appears on 18 of the 66 days, with distinct stories on the FTA CBAM annex, the exporter awareness session, EEPC's supplier-data demand, UK recognition of CCTS, the BRICS opposition, verifier registry access, the WTO dispute and 'carbon cash home'.
- BRSR, SSA 5000, PCAF, SBTi, CSRD and GRI appear on 0 days.
- Caveat: the feed set is markets, economy and top stories, so trade topics are over-represented.
(3) Competitor content visible on GitHub:
- Syntropy Earth's llms.txt shows a small Indian advisory already publishing on BRSR Core assessment vs assurance, CSRD after Omnibus I, and a glossary.
- An EU importer site (Kinzoku) publishes India CBAM default-value content.
- Acquis has an India CBAM cost dashboard, and a third-party JSW actual-vs-default case study exists.
- A Hinglish CA-update site covered SSA 5000 on 21 Sep 2026.
- CCTS-745 (CC BY, created 29 Jul 2026, 0 stars) has no SEO front end.

Regulatory checks I could make first-hand:
- G.S.R. 739(E) and draft G.S.R. 517(E) are MoEFCC notifications, and the steel schedule is still marked DRAFT in the gazette text. Note that the CCTS-745 README wrongly says 'Ministry of Power'; do not copy it.
- UK CBAM from 1 Jan 2027 in five sectors is corroborated by the EU Climate Advisory Board's dataset.
- SSA 5000's effective date (FYs from 1 Apr 2027) comes only from a secondary site.
- Whether the steel CCTS targets have been finalised could NOT be verified.

CROSS-CUTTING OBSERVATIONS (lens: organic opportunity for a young domain):
1. A domain with no backlinks wins first through structured, refreshable data that answers entity-level long-tail queries and earns links. Head terms ('BRSR', 'CBAM India', 'best BRSR software') are infeasible in the near term.
   - The strongest organic engines are C17 (per-entity CCTS pages), C12 (per-factor-family pages), C24 (per-CN-code pages), C18 (per-plant steel lookup) and C01 (per-company BRSR Core pages, which only work if ungated).
   - Commercial guides should then hang off these pillars.
2. Several candidates are really cluster posts, not separate pillars. Consolidate to avoid cannibalisation:
   - BRSR Core assurance pillar: C02 + C03 + C13 (+ C04).
   - CBAM exporter pillar: C24 + C25 + C26 + C30.
   - Interplay pillar: C27 + C28 + C29.
   - CCTS pillar: C17 + C18 + C19 + C20 + C21.
   - Benchmark dataset: C01 + C10 + C05 share one parse.
3. MISSING high-demand, feasible topics:
   - 'BRSR format Excel / template download' and 'BRSR XBRL filing utility how-to' (transactional, seasonal Jun-Sep).
   - 'CBAM communication template for installations explained'.
   - A live 'carbon credit certificate price India' tracker for when CCC trading starts (start date unverified).
   - 'Indian Carbon Market portal registration' how-to (every obligated entity must register).
   - Programmatic '<company> BRSR FY2025-26' pages.
   - Hindi/Hinglish versions for MSME, CCTS-textile and CA audiences (Hinglish coverage already exists for SSA 5000).
4. The off-core topics C38, C39, C43 and C44 would dilute topical authority without realistic ranking prospects.
5. Brand-SERP hygiene comes before any of this. ESG Astraa's own CCTS post states 'nine sectors' against PIB's 'seven' and needs a dated update. Publish every asset with ungated HTML, keyword slugs (not /insights/blogs/2), dated 'last verified' stamps and Organization/Article/FAQ schema, or none of these papers will rank.

VERIFICATION LIMITS (read first): I could not spot-check live answer engines or SERPs this session. WebSearch returned "budget exhausted (200 of 200)". Firecrawl returned HTTP 402 (out of credits; the user needs to add credits). The egress proxy blocked WebFetch and curl to every non-GitHub host I tried, including google.com, duckduckgo, brave, bing, sebi.gov.in, pib.gov.in, cea.nic.in, eur-lex, competitor sites (thesustainabilitycloud.com, climes.io, relific.io) and Indian news sites. So no live AI answer, PAA box, autocomplete or search volume was observed, and no demand figure below is measured. Where I talk about demand, it is an ESTIMATE from proxies: how often a question recurs across the supplied VoC question list, how crowded the competitor content is, and how much news it gets.

What I could check, via GitHub only:
- (a) Competitor syntropyearth already has a dated (2 Sep 2026) answer-capsule page that correctly answers "is reasonable assurance still mandatory / assessment vs assurance". It also notes that BRSR Section A points 14-15 now name the provider and the type of check. That makes the C01 statistic extractable, but it weakens C02's novelty. https://github.com/syntropyearth/syntropyearth-site/blob/HEAD/thinking/brsr-core-assessment-or-assurance-sebi/index.html
- (b) An open CC BY dataset, CCTS-745, already exists. Its README attributes the gazettes to the "Ministry of Power" and lists draft Phase III (G.S.R. 517(E)) alongside the notified phases. So there is a correctable, citable error, but also a free alternative. https://github.com/prakulhiremath/ccts-745
- (c) India CBAM default values from IR 2026/1740 (EC Excel v2, 6 Aug 2026) are already republished as an open CSV and an MCP tool. Examples: 7601 unwrought aluminium 1.87, 7203 DRI 4.2, and 7207 semi-finished steel 4.27 tCO2e/t, with 10/20/30% mark-ups. https://github.com/Meetv9/ecosetu.cbam/blob/main/data/india_cbam_defaults.csv and https://github.com/Keremozdemirra/cbam-mcp
- (d) A CC0 'Open India Emission Factors' database (v1.3, 5 Aug 2026; 116 factors including 51 CEA V21 grid factors) exists but is labelled AI-extracted and unverified. https://github.com/Creator619-Python/open-india-emission-factors

final.strategy_summary:
ESG Astraa ranks today only for its brand and one timely CCTS news post. Answer engines leave it out of every category answer, and some describe it as a GitHub build package. A young domain with no backlinks will not win head terms ('BRSR software', 'CBAM India') in 2026-27. It can win by publishing the reference data that India's compliance deadlines force people to look up and that nobody publishes cleanly: facility-level CCTS targets, India's CBAM default values by CN code, and filing-level BRSR Core assurance data.

SHARED DATASETS. The 20 papers rest on four shared datasets, so the research load is four builds, not twenty:
(1) a gazette parse of all 745 CCTS entities;
(2) India's CBAM default-value table under IR 2026/1740;
(3) a BRSR XBRL parse of the top 1,000;
(4) a BRSR-CCTS-CBAM field crosswalk.

WEIGHTING. The mix follows the product's 'Sell CBAM first' wedge and its steel ideal customer. 13 of the 20 papers sit in CCTS, CBAM or their overlap, timed to the January-September 2027 deadline cluster:
- 1 Jan: CBAM default mark-up rises to 20%
- 1 Feb: certificate sales open
- 31 Mar: CCTS FY2026-27 year-end
- 1 Apr: SSA 5000 takes effect
- 30 Sep: first CBAM surrender
The 7 BRSR papers serve the land-and-expand motion and earn press and links.

P1 (October-December 2026, 8 papers):
- the two flagship datasets (C17, C24)
- the papers that use them for the Q4 contract window (C26, C27, C18)
- the BRSR tracker while FY2025-26 filings are fresh (C01)
- two fast explainers whose windows close quickly (C04 on SSA 5000, C28 on the CCTS-CBAM deduction)

SWAPS from the composite ranking:
- C21 replaces C31 (UK vs EU CBAM). C31 is folded into C28 as a chapter. C21 is expanded into a guide to the first CCTS compliance cycle, covering ICM portal registration and the true-up, which the judges flagged as missing.
- C20 replaces C35 (multi-jurisdiction disclosure calendar). C35 would generate leads for regimes the product does not serve.

CREDIBILITY RULES for a pre-launch vendor:
- Base every hook on public data plus clearly labelled 'illustrative' Novaferro examples.
- Make no platform-telemetry claims until there are users.
- Position ESG Astraa as a readiness and data partner, never as an assessor or verifier.
- Before launch, fix the blog's 'nine sectors' line, and remove or substantiate the '70% faster BRSR' homepage claim.
- Make the public GitHub mirror private or rewrite it.

ONLINE CHECKS RUN TODAY (1 Oct 2026). The WebSearch budget was exhausted, Firecrawl returned 402, and only GitHub was reachable.
- I re-parsed the three CCTS gazette PDFs (via the CCTS-745 repo). Confirmed: the issuer is MoEFCC, not the Ministry of Power; G.S.R. 739(E) is dated 8 Oct 2025 (282 entities); G.S.R. 25(E) is dated 13 Jan 2026 (208 entities); G.S.R. 517(E) is dated 26 Jun 2026 (255 entities) and is still marked 'DRAFT NOTIFICATION'; Rule 6 sets compensation at twice the average CCC price, payable within 90 days.
- The parse reproduces the C17 hook: 839.1 MtCO2e baseline; 36.7 Mt do-nothing shortfall at FY2026-27 targets; 310 of 745 entities below 10,000 t; top 10% hold 64.6%. It also shows 457 entities in CBAM sectors, and 65 of the 490 notified entities with no FY2025-26 target. Two PDF rows needed manual fixes, so a second check is required before publication.
- From a mirror of the Commission's Excel v2, India's CBAM default for CN 7208 flat-rolled steel is 4.28 tCO2e/t, or 5.136 with the 2027 mark-up. That contradicts the 'illustrative 2.5' figure circulating online.
- News digests to 1 Oct 2026 show no report that CCC trading has started or that the steel targets are final; both remain unverified.
- Two fixes for the product docs: the Phase II date should read 13 Jan 2026, not 16 Jan; and the line 'ICAI has not adopted ISSA 5000' is superseded by SSA 5000 (reported by secondary sources; primary ICAI text not read).

whitepapers.subtitle: Covers the 490 notified entities in seven sectors plus 255 iron and steel plants in draft G.S.R. 517(E). For each: baseline, FY2025-26 and FY2026-27 targets, do-nothing shortfall and CCC price scenarios, every figure cited to its gazette page.

whitepapers.thesis: India's compliance carbon market is now a named list of plants, published only as gazette PDF tables. The one open consolidation misattributes the gazettes to the Ministry of Power and mixes draft Phase III with notified phases. A versioned, gazette-cited atlas becomes the default reference for every 'is my plant covered / what is my target' question. It also quantifies exposure for the first time. Across 745 entities (490 notified plus 255 steel in draft) the FY2023-24 baseline is about 839 MtCO2e, and the do-nothing shortfall at FY2026-27 targets is about 36.7 Mt. That shortfall is concentrated: the top 10% of entities hold about 65%. Yet 310 entities face do-nothing shortfalls below 10,000 t. The argument: for most obligated entities CCTS is first a data-and-evidence problem, where the cost of MRV exceeds the cost of carbon; for a few dozen it is a balance-sheet problem. Each group needs a different response.

whitepapers.thesis: CBAM default values are a penalty price for missing data, and the penalty rises every year. India's listed default for flat-rolled steel (CN 7208) is 4.28 tCO2e/t before mark-up, and 5.136 with the 20% mark-up that applies from 1 Jan 2027. The paper builds the authoritative CN-code-by-route table from the Commission's Excel v2 and IR 2026/1740. It models certificate cost under the CBAM-factor phase-in and three price paths, and computes the break-even at which installation-level MRV and verification pay for themselves. The conclusion for most Indian producers: measuring is cheaper than defaulting, and the exporter who brings a verified number keeps the order.

whitepapers.thesis:
The EU importer is CBAM's legal declarant, but the Indian exporter bears much of the cost through price. EU buyers are budgeting now for 2027:
- certificate sales open on 1 Feb 2027
- importers must hold 50% of their quarterly obligation
- prices are published weekly from 2027
- the default-value mark-up doubles to 20%
They are asking for concessions, which GTRI puts at 15-22%. The paper argues exporters should negotiate on data, not price. A verified actual-emissions figure, contractual data sharing, an agreed split of verification cost and a pass-through formula tied to the buyer's real certificate cost are worth more than a blanket discount. It gives the CFO a working model: liability per tonne under default and actual values, cash-flow timing, provisioning and board disclosure.

whitepapers.thesis:
457 of the 745 CCTS entities make CBAM goods: 16 aluminium, 186 cement including grinding units, and 255 iron and steel in draft. Each must report two different figures:
- for CCTS, a GEI per tonne of equivalent product, on a financial year, using BEE methods, verified by an ACVA
- for CBAM, a specific embedded emission per tonne of good, on a calendar year, including precursors, using EU methods, verified by an EU-accredited verifier
The two numbers will differ, and the first CBAM verifications in 2027 will expose any inconsistency. The paper shows the gap can be explained and reconciled from one activity-data ledger, item by item: boundary, period, product definition, electricity treatment and factors. A documented reconciliation is an audit asset, not a spreadsheet chore. This is the clearest expression of ESG Astraa's 'one store' thesis.
